extName.description: Extension name, shown in the browser's extension list and the store. 'Global Privacy Control' is the name of a web standard; keep the acronym 'GPC'.

extDescription.message: Reports whether GPC was enabled, what the site did with it, who read it, and what was sent to third parties.
extDescription.description: Short description of the extension, shown in the store listing and the browser's extension list. 132 characters at most. Says what the extension reports and makes no judgment about sites. Use a plain word for 'sent': not a word meaning 'shared' or 'sold', which are legal terms in US privacy law.

tabOverview.description: Tab label for the main results view.

tabRequests.description: Tab label for the list of HTTP requests the page made. Followed by a request count.

signalSetBy.message: Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal is set
signalSetBy.description: First line of the popup when a GPC signal is set; a short tag saying who set it follows (sourceThisExtension, sourceBrowser, sourceOtherExtension). The only place the acronym is spelled out, so every later string can say 'GPC' alone. 'Global Privacy Control' is the standard's name: translate the words, keep the acronym.

signalNotSet.message: Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal is not set
signalNotSet.description: First line of the popup when no GPC signal is set; a tag saying why can follow (such as sourceBrowserOff). Spells out the acronym, as signalSetBy does. A known negative: keep it distinct from sourceUnknown, which says the state could not be determined.

sourceThisExtension.description: Tag after signalSetBy: this extension set the signal. Lowercase; it continues the line.

sourceBrowser.description: Tag after signalSetBy: the browser itself sets the signal, so the extension only observes. Lowercase; it continues the line.

sourceOtherExtension.description: Tag after signalSetBy: a different extension sets the signal. The extension cannot tell which one, so the tag names none. Lowercase; it continues the line.

sourceBrowserOff.description: Tag after signalNotSet: the browser supports GPC and has it turned off, and this extension is not sending its own header. Not the same as sourceOffInSettings, which is this extension's own setting.

sourceOtherExtensionOff.description: Tag after signalNotSet: a different extension controls the GPC property and has it off, and this extension is not sending its own header. The extension cannot tell which one, so the tag names none.

sourceBrowserOffHeaderSent.message: turned off in the browser, but this extension still sends the Sec-GPC header
sourceBrowserOffHeaderSent.description: Tag after signalNotSet: the browser has GPC turned off, so page scripts read it as off, while this extension still sends its Sec-GPC request header to sites. 'Sec-GPC' is an HTTP header name: never translate it.

sourceOtherExtensionOffHeaderSent.message: turned off by another extension, but this extension still sends the Sec-GPC header
sourceOtherExtensionOffHeaderSent.description: As sourceBrowserOffHeaderSent, when a different extension controls the GPC property and has it off. 'Sec-GPC' is an HTTP header name: never translate it.

sourceOffInSettings.description: Tag after signalNotSet: the user turned sending off in this extension's settings. A choice, not a failure.

sectionSiteDid.description: Section heading on the Overview over the rows about the site: who read GPC, whether the site publishes a GPC file, and whether the page showed a GPC confirmation. 'Did' covers both what happened on this visit and what the site states.

sectionPrivacyStrings.description: Section heading over the GPP, US Privacy, TCF and Google Consent Mode rows. One of the few places the general term 'privacy strings' is used; elsewhere each string is named (GPP, USP, TCF). Plural: it heads the whole set. Translate it the same way in firstRunBody and reportStep1, which name this section.

sectionPrivacyStringsDesc.message: What this site reports to third parties about your opt-out state.
sectionPrivacyStringsDesc.description: Line under the Privacy strings heading. The only place that says what these strings are: data the site passes to third parties about the reader's opt-out choices.

labelCheckedForGpc.description: Group heading on the Overview over the three GPC read rows (labelReadObserved, labelReadNotObserved, labelReadUndetermined): whether scripts on the page read the GPC signal, and which. 'Read' covers two observable acts: a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl, or a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp). 'From the page' limits the claim: servers can act on the Sec-GPC request header, which no extension can see. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

labelReadObserved.description: First of the GPC read rows under 'Read GPC from the page': the vendors whose scripts were observed reading GPC, listed under the label, or 'none' (valueReadNone). Always shown. Pairs with 'No read observed' (labelReadNotObserved): translate the two so they differ by one word.

labelReadNotObserved.description: Second of the GPC read rows under 'Read GPC from the page': the vendors on the page with no read of GPC observed, listed under the label, or 'none'. Always shown. Same words as the vendor state vendorGpcNotRead. Never 'did not read': servers can act on the Sec-GPC header, which no extension can see.

labelReadUndetermined.description: Third of the GPC read rows under 'Read GPC from the page', shown only when a vendor is in this state: whether the vendor read GPC cannot be determined, usually because the read came from inside a tag container. Same words as the vendor state vendorGpcCheckUnattributable.

valueReadNone.description: Value of a GPC read row with no vendor in it. Lowercase, like the section's other values ('yes', 'no', 'checking'). A hint line under the row can still name a tag container or a domain.

vendorInCategory.description: A vendor as the GPC read rows list it: the company's name, then the category of its domains that the row is about. The same company can appear in two rows with two categories. $NAME$ is the company name from the classification list, never translated. $CATEGORY$ is a category label that is already translated (a category_ message or categoryUncategorized). Also used in a tag container's panel ('Vendors loaded', 'Requests sent to') and in the saved summary. Everything after the name is drawn in a lighter color, so keep the name first if your language allows.

hintCheckedOtherDomains.description: Hint line under 'Read observed': scripts that read GPC and belong to no vendor row, named by the domain they came from. $DOMAINS$ is a comma-separated list of domains, the site's own first (formatted by hintCheckedThisSite), then alphabetical. Domains are never translated. No closing period: the line ends on a domain, where a period would read as part of the name.

hintCheckedThisSite.description: The site's own domain inside the hintCheckedOtherDomains list, marked as this site. $DOMAIN$ is the domain, never translated.

hintGppCalledUnidentified.message: A script also read GPC through the GPP consent API but could not be identified.
hintGppCalledUnidentified.description: Hint line under 'Read observed': a call to the GPP consent API was observed, and the script that made it could not be identified.

hintReadsNoneTraced.message: GPC was read but could not be traced to a script.
hintReadsNoneTraced.description: Hint line under 'Read observed' when GPC reads were counted but none could be traced to a vendor, a container or another script. Without it, 'none' on the row would read as nothing having read GPC.

hintReadsUnidentified.message: A script also read the GPC property but could not be identified.
hintReadsUnidentified.description: Hint line under 'Read observed' when at least one read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl came from a script that could not be identified (bundled, inline or generated code), while other reads were traced. The counterpart of hintGppCalledUnidentified, for property reads. When no read was traced to anything, hintReadsNoneTraced is shown instead.

hintCheckedTagManagerAlso.message: One or more tags in a tag container also read it.
hintCheckedTagManagerAlso.description: Hint line under 'Read observed', after named vendors: a read was traced into a tag container whose id is not known. Which tag in it read cannot be determined. 'It' is GPC. With a known id, hintCheckedContainerAlso or hintCheckedContainersAlso is used. 'Tag container' is the popup's term for these tools; use it consistently.

hintCheckedContainerAlso.message: One or more tags in $ID$ also read it.
hintCheckedContainerAlso.description: Hint line under 'Read observed', after named vendors: a read was traced into the tag container $ID$. Which tag in it read cannot be determined. 'It' is GPC. $ID$ is a container id, never translated. Plural: hintCheckedContainersAlso.

hintCheckedContainersAlso.message: One or more tags in $IDS$ also read it.
hintCheckedContainersAlso.description: Plural of hintCheckedContainerAlso: reads were traced into two or more tag containers. $IDS$ is a comma-separated list of container ids, never translated.

hintCheckedContainerRead.message: One or more tags in $ID$ read it.
hintCheckedContainerRead.description: Hint line under 'Read observed' when no vendor is named on the row, so there is no 'also': reads were traced into the tag container $ID$. 'It' is GPC. $ID$ is a container id, never translated. Plural: hintCheckedContainersRead.

hintCheckedContainersRead.message: One or more tags in $IDS$ read it.
hintCheckedContainersRead.description: Plural of hintCheckedContainerRead: reads were traced into two or more tag containers. $IDS$ is a comma-separated list of container ids, never translated.

hintCheckedTagManagerRead.message: One or more tags in a tag container read it.
hintCheckedTagManagerRead.description: As hintCheckedContainerRead, when the container's id is not known.

hintNoCheckGppRecords.message: The site's GPP string has the GPC field set, but no script was observed reading it.
hintNoCheckGppRecords.description: Hint line at the bottom of the GPC read rows, when the site's GPP string has its GPC field set and no script was observed reading GPC. The string is context, not evidence that anything acted on it. 'GPC field' is the field in the GPP string; translate it as in gppFieldGpc.

hintGppStringSilent.message: The site's GPP string does not have the GPC field set.
hintGppStringSilent.description: Hint line at the bottom of the GPC read rows, when a script called the GPP consent API while the signal was on and the site's GPP string has no GPC field set. A fact about the site's string, which the Privacy strings section decodes.

hintReadsUnavailable.message: GPC property reads could not be observed on this page.
hintReadsUnavailable.description: Hint line under 'No read observed' when reads of the GPC property could not be counted on this page (the browser or another extension controls the property). Scripts can still read it; only the extension's count is missing.

hintReadsCapped.message: GPC reads exceeded the tracing cap. Later reads were not traced to a script.
hintReadsCapped.description: Hint line under 'No read observed' on a page that went past the limit on traced GPC reads: a vendor listed there may have read GPC after the limit. A fact about the measurement, not about the vendors. The limit is the 'Limit GPC read tracing' setting (settingReadTraceCap).

labelPrivacyString.description: Row label in Privacy strings for the GPP string. Leads with the full name because the acronym alone means nothing to most readers. IAB's product name: keep the acronym 'GPP', and translate the words only if your language has an established name for it.

nameGpp.description: Full name of GPP, shown when the row is expanded. IAB's name for the standard: do not translate.

valueGpcFieldYes.description: First half of the closed GPP row's value: the string's GPC field is 1, meaning the site's consent manager recorded that it received the GPC signal. Say 'GPC field', never 'GPC detected': the field is what is reported, and 'detected' reads as the extension's own observation.

valueGpcFieldNo.description: First half of the closed GPP row's value: the string's GPC field is 0, meaning the consent manager recorded that it did not receive GPC. Not the same as valueGpcFieldAbsent, where the string has no GPC field.

valueGpcFieldAbsent.description: First half of the closed GPP row's value: the string has no GPC field at all. Common, and not the same as a recorded 0 (valueGpcFieldNo).

valueGppOptedOut.description: Second half of the closed GPP row's value: at least one opt-out field is 1 (opted out) and none is 2. When one is 1 and another is 2, valueGppOptedOutSome is used.

valueGppOptedOutSome.description: Second half of the closed GPP row's value: one opt-out field is 1 (opted out) and another is 2 (did not opt out). The expanded row shows which.

valueGppNotOptedOut.description: Second half of the closed GPP row's value: the opt-out fields are 2 (did not opt out). In IAB's encoding 2 means 'did not opt out', which is why the number is never shown alone.

valueGppNoOptOut.description: Second half of the closed GPP row's value: the opt-out fields are 0 or absent, so the string states no opt-out either way.

valueGppWireOnly.description: Whole value of the closed GPP row when the page reported no GPP string and an outbound request carried a valid one. The lines in the expanded row show each string and the host it went to. Same words as valueUspWireOnly. Not the same as 'not present' (no string anywhere) or 'not observable' (the extension could not watch the page's GPP API).

valueGppNoUsSection.description: Whole value of the closed GPP row: the string has sections, but no US state section. Never 'no opt-out recorded': the string had no field that could record one.

valueGppUsSectionNoFields.message: US section named, no fields reported
valueGppUsSectionNoFields.description: Whole value of the closed GPP row: the string names a US state section, but the consent manager reported no fields for it, so there is no opt-out or GPC field to decode. The expanded row lists the sections named.

gppNoUsSectionNote.message: This string has no US state section, so there is no opt-out or GPC field to show.
gppNoUsSectionNote.description: Note in the expanded GPP row when the string has no US state section and no US Privacy section, and has at least one consent section of another kind (such as the EU or Canadian TCF).

gppOnlyLegacyUsNote.message: This string has no US state section (section 7 and up), only the older US Privacy section (section 6).
gppOnlyLegacyUsNote.description: Note in the expanded GPP row when the string has the older US Privacy section (section 6) and no US state section. The US Privacy row below decodes the same opt-out from the page's other sources. Keep the section numbers.

valueStringNotReadable.description: GPP or US Privacy row value: a string arrived that the extension could not decode. Does not say the string is malformed, which would be a verdict on the site. The raw value is shown so a reader can judge.

gppFieldGpc.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the value of the string's own GPC field, with the raw IAB number beside it. Same name as the closed row's 'GPC field: yes' (valueGpcFieldYes), because it is a field of the string.

gppGroupOptOut.description: Group heading in the expanded GPP row, over the sale, sharing and targeted advertising fields.

valueOptOutNoneRecorded.description: Shown beside the Opt-out heading in the expanded GPP row when no field records an opt-out.

gppLabelSection.description: Label in the expanded GPP row for one GPP section: the US state or national section the row decodes, such as 'US - California (8)', or the one section listed when there is no US state section. IAB's own term. Plural: gppLabelSections.

gppLabelSections.description: Plural of gppLabelSection, for the row listing every section a GPP string carries.

valueYes.description: Generic row value: yes. Lowercase, like the other row values.

valueNo.description: Generic row value: no. Lowercase, like the other row values.

gppFieldSaleOptOut.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's SaleOptOut field, in plain words.

gppFieldSharingOptOut.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's SharingOptOut field, in plain words.

gppFieldTargetedAdvertisingOptOut.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's TargetedAdvertisingOptOut field, in plain words.

gppFieldSaleOptOutNotice.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's SaleOptOutNotice field, whether the site says it gave notice of the right to opt out of sale.

gppFieldSharingOptOutNotice.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's SharingOptOutNotice field, whether the site says it gave notice of the right to opt out of sharing.

gppFieldTargetedAdvertisingOptOutNotice.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's TargetedAdvertisingOptOutNotice field, whether the site says it gave notice of the right to opt out of targeted advertising.

gppFieldMspaCoveredTransaction.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's MspaCoveredTransaction field. MSPA is the IAB Multi-State Privacy Agreement; keep the acronym.

gppFieldMspaServiceProviderMode.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's MspaServiceProviderMode field. Keep the acronym MSPA.

gppFieldMspaOptOutOptionMode.description: Row in the expanded GPP row: the string's MspaOptOutOptionMode field. Keep the acronym MSPA.

valueOptedOut.description: Value of a GPP opt-out field that is 1. In IAB's encoding 1 means the person opted out.

valueNotOptedOut.description: Value of a GPP opt-out field that is 2. In IAB's encoding 2 means the person did not opt out, although the larger number is the weaker state.

valueFieldNotApplicable.description: Value of a GPP field that is 0: the field does not apply. A value the string states, not something the extension could not see.

valueNoticeProvided.description: Value of a GPP notice field that is 1: notice was provided.

valueNoticeNotProvided.description: Value of a GPP notice field that is 2: notice was not provided.

labelUsPrivacy.description: Row label in Privacy strings for the older US Privacy string. Leads with the full name, as the GPP and TCF rows do. A dimmed 'deprecated' (labelDeprecated) sits beside it. Keep the acronym 'USP'.

nameUsp.description: Full name of USP, shown when the row is expanded. Do not translate.

labelDeprecated.description: Dimmed word beside the US Privacy row label: IAB has deprecated this string. Lowercase.

valueUspOptedOutY.description: Closed US Privacy row value: the string's third character is Y (opted out of sale). Lowercase: a row value, not a sentence.

valueUspOptedOutN.description: Closed US Privacy row value: the string's third character is N (did not opt out of sale). Lowercase.

valueUspNotApplicable.description: Closed US Privacy row value: the string's third character is '-', meaning the site states the opt-out does not apply. Only for a real '-'; an unreadable string shows valueStringNotReadable, because the two are different claims.

labelRawString.description: Label on the raw encoded string at the foot of an expanded privacy string row. Lowercase: it labels a value, not a section.

uspLabelVersion.description: Row in the expanded US Privacy row, for the string's first character: the US Privacy specification version.

uspLabelNotice.description: Row in the expanded US Privacy row, for the string's second character: whether the site says it gave the required notice.

uspLabelOptOut.description: Row in the expanded US Privacy row, for the string's third character: whether the person opted out of sale.

uspLabelLspa.description: Row in the expanded US Privacy row, for the string's fourth character: whether the transaction is covered by the IAB Limited Service Provider Agreement.

hintUspDeprecated.message: Deprecated by IAB as of Jan 31, 2024, in favor of GPP. Some vendors still use it.
hintUspDeprecated.description: Note at the top of the expanded US Privacy row: who deprecated the string, when, and what replaced it. Keep 'IAB' and 'GPP'. Write the date in your language's usual format.

labelTcf.description: Row label in Privacy strings for TCF. Leads with the full name, as the GPP and US Privacy rows do. IAB Europe's framework: keep the acronym 'TCF'. A dimmed 'EU / GDPR' (labelTcfScope) sits beside it, so it never reads as a response to GPC.

nameTcf.description: Full name of TCF, shown when the row is expanded. Do not translate.

labelTcfScope.description: Dimmed qualifier beside the TCF row label. Use the acronyms your language uses for the EU and the GDPR.

tcfScopeNote.message: A GDPR consent framework. Separate from GPC and not a response to it.
tcfScopeNote.description: Note at the top of the expanded TCF row. TCF is a GDPR consent framework with no link to GPC; this line keeps it from reading as a response to GPC.

valueTcfGranted.description: Closed TCF row value: how many of the purposes the consent manager listed have consent granted, two or more. $GRANTED$ is that number. Singular: valueTcfGrantedOne. None: valueTcfNoneGranted. The expanded row lists each purpose.

valueTcfGrantedOne.description: Singular of valueTcfGranted: exactly one listed purpose has consent granted.

valueTcfNoneGranted.description: Closed TCF row value: the consent manager listed purposes and none has consent granted. Not the same as valueTcfNoPurposes, where it listed none.

rowConsentMode.description: Row label in Privacy strings: the consent state Google's tags on the page run under, read from Google's own consent store. One store serves every Google tag on the page, so it is a fact about the page. 'Google Consent Mode' is Google's product name: keep it whole, with 'Google' as part of the name.

valueConsentGranted.description: Closed Google Consent Mode row value: how many of Google's four consent types (ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization, analytics_storage) are granted. $N$ is that number. Counts consent types only, never storage types. Values are never colored: granted is not good and denied is not bad.

valueConsentNotSet.description: Closed Google Consent Mode row value when Google's tags ran and none of the four consent types has a value. The row opens to say so and to list each type as not set. Not the same as 'no Google tags' (valueConsentNoGoogleTags).

valueConsentNoGoogleTags.description: Google Consent Mode row value when the page ran no Google tag. The row does not open. Lowercase: it reads as a value.

valueConsentUnread.description: Google Consent Mode row value when Google's tags ran and the extension could not read their consent state. Something the extension could not look at, so it never says 'not set'. The row does not open.

valueConsentTypeNotSet.description: Value of one consent or storage type in the expanded Google Consent Mode row, when nothing gave it a value. Drawn as an absence.

consentNoneSetNote.message: No consent types were set for Google's tags
consentNoneSetNote.description: The one sentence in the expanded Google Consent Mode row, under 'Consent types', shown only when the row reads 'not set'.

consentGroupTypes.description: Heading in the expanded Google Consent Mode row over Google's four consent types, which control whether its tags run and what they send.

consentGroupStorage.description: Heading in the expanded Google Consent Mode row over Google's three storage types (functionality_storage, personalization_storage, security_storage). Not counted in the closed row's value.

valueGranted.description: Value in the expanded TCF and Google Consent Mode rows: consent for this purpose or type was granted. Never colored: granted is not good and denied is not bad.

valueDenied.description: Value in the expanded TCF and Google Consent Mode rows: consent for this purpose or type was denied.

tcfLabelGdprApplies.description: Row in the expanded TCF row: whether the consent manager indicated that the GDPR applies to this visitor.

valueTcfNoPurposes.description: TCF row value: a TCF string arrived and its consent manager listed no purposes. 'Reported', not 'decoded': there was nothing to decode, and 'decoded' would read as the extension's failure. Listed purposes with none granted show valueTcfNoneGranted.

linkTcfDecoder.description: Link in the expanded TCF row to IAB's public decoder, which opens with the string filled in. Same destination and words as linkGppDecoder. 'iabgpp.com' is a site address: never translate it. Keep the arrow.

linkGppDecoder.description: Link in the expanded GPP row to IAB's public encoder and decoder, which opens with the string filled in. Names its destination so the reader knows where it goes. 'iabgpp.com' is a site address: never translate it. Keep the arrow.

labelConfirmation.description: Row label in 'What this site did': whether the page displayed a notice that it processed the GPC signal. Values: yes, no, checking. 'Shown on page' is the scope of the claim: a site may confirm elsewhere, such as in account settings, which the extension cannot see. Names GPC so it cannot be read as a cookie banner or an order confirmation.

valueNotPresent.description: Row value: the extension looked and the item was absent. A fact about the site. Keep distinct from 'not observable' (valueNotObservable).

valueChecking.description: Row value while a check has started and not finished: the request for the site's GPC file is still waiting, or the page has not yet reported its confirmation scan. A transition, not an absence: keep it distinct from 'not found', which means the extension looked. Lowercase.

valueTcfGdprNotApplies.description: TCF row value when the page's consent manager answered that the GDPR does not apply and gave no consent string.

tcfGdprNotAppliesNote.message: The page's consent manager answered that GDPR does not apply to this visit.
tcfGdprNotAppliesNote.description: Sentence in the expanded TCF row for valueTcfGdprNotApplies. 'Consent manager' is the page's consent management platform; use the same term as elsewhere in the popup.

hintWellKnownStatus.description: Added after the checked address under 'Declares GPC support: not found' when the server answered with an error status. $STATUS$ is the HTTP status number. It tells a 403 from bot protection, for example, apart from a 404. Keep the leading dot separator.

hintWellKnownNoResponse.description: Added after the checked address under 'Declares GPC support: could not be checked' when the request for the file got no answer (a timeout, a network error, or a redirect whose target was never reported). Keep the leading dot separator.

countCookies.message: third-party cookies set by advertising or analytics domains while your GPC signal was on
countCookies.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Plural. Used when no counted cookie belongs to a named vendor; otherwise a countCookiesBy caption is used. 'Third-party' is stated so that the first-party line below it (countFirstPartyVendor) reads as a different measure. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesOne.message: third-party cookie set by an advertising or analytics domain while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesOne.description: Singular of countCookies: the count above is 1. Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. 'Third-party' is stated so that the first-party line below it (countFirstPartyVendor) reads as a different measure. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesZero.message: No third-party cookies set by advertising or analytics vendors while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesZero.description: Headline when no counted cookie was set while the GPC signal was on. A full sentence with no number. Also shown when advertising or analytics domains were contacted and set no counted cookie, so it must not read as 'no vendors were present'. 'Third-party' is stated so that the first-party line below it (countFirstPartyVendor) reads as a different measure. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

sectionVendors.description: Section heading on the Overview over the vendor rows. The rows are grouped by category, each group headed by the category's name (the category_ messages).

sectionTagContainers.description: Section heading on the Overview, under Vendors, over the site's tag containers: one row per container, and one row for every Google tag id. Also a heading in the saved summary. 'Tag container' is the popup's term for tag management tools and the Google tag; use it consistently.

sectionFirstParty.description: Last section heading on the Overview, after Tag containers: cookies charged to the site itself, set by its own responses or written by scripts it serves from its own domain. Nothing in it is counted. A noun phrase, matching the Requests tab's party label 'First party' (groupFirstParty). Also a heading in the saved summary.

firstPartyIntro.message: Cookies set by this site's own responses or by scripts it serves from its own domain. A cookie set inside a tag container is listed under Tag containers, and one a third-party script sets on this site's domain is listed under that third party.
firstPartyIntro.description: Opening sentence of the First party section's panel. Says which cookies are listed here and which are listed elsewhere: a cookie belongs to whoever set it, so a third-party script setting a cookie on the site's domain is listed under that third party, and anything set inside a tag container is listed under Tag containers. 'Set' covers cookies from responses and from scripts.

firstPartyListVendor.message: Written by the site's advertising or analytics scripts
firstPartyListVendor.description: Label over the first of the First party panel's two lists: cookies written by scripts the site serves from its own domain where the classification list puts that host in Advertising or Analytics. The same cookies the first-party line under the count counts (countFirstPartyVendor); not in the main count.

firstPartyListSite.message: Set by the site's responses or other scripts
firstPartyListSite.description: Label over the second of the First party panel's two lists: every other cookie charged to the site, set by its responses or written by its other scripts. Not counted.

containersColumnCheckTitle.message: Whether a tag inside this container read GPC on the page. Which tag cannot be determined.
containersColumnCheckTitle.description: Hover text on the 'Read GPC' column heading of the Tag containers section (the heading reuses vendorsColumnCheck). Says what a container's state answers, and the limit that always applies: a read inside a container is traced to the container, never to one tag.

containerNameGoogleTag.description: Row name for the Google tag (gtag.js) in the Tag containers section. Every Google tag id on the page shares this row. Google's product name: follow Google's own usage in your language. Other products (Google Tag Manager, Tealium, Adobe Launch) are brand names and are not messages.

containerTagRead.description: A container's state in the 'Read GPC' column: a read of GPC came from inside the container. Leads with 'a tag' because which tag made the read cannot be determined; the row never names one. Use the same verb 'read' as the rest of the popup.

containerNoRead.description: A container's state in the 'Read GPC' column: read tracing covered the whole page and no read came from inside the container. Same words as the vendor state vendorGpcNotRead. An observation: it never claims the container does not act on GPC, since a tag's server can act on the Sec-GPC header.

containerCannotDetermine.description: A container's state in the 'Read GPC' column when read tracing was limited on this page or could not run, so the lack of a read is not an observation. Keep it distinct from 'No read observed'.

containerTagReadHelp.message: A tag in this container read GPC. Which tag cannot be determined.
containerTagReadHelp.description: Opening sentence of a container's panel, and hover text on its state, for 'A tag read GPC'. The second sentence is the limit that always applies: the extension cannot tell which tag in a container made a read.

containerNoReadHelp.message: No GPC read from this container.
containerNoReadHelp.description: Opening sentence of a container's panel, and hover text on its state, for 'No read observed'. One sentence for every container product.

containerCannotDetermineHelp.message: GPC reads on this page were traced only in part. A read from this container may have been missed.
containerCannotDetermineHelp.description: Opening sentence of a container's panel, and hover text on its state, for 'Cannot determine' when the page went past the limit on traced GPC reads. Says why the state is not 'No read observed'.

containerCannotDetermineHelpOff.message: GPC reads on this page could not be traced. Whether a tag in this container read GPC cannot be determined.
containerCannotDetermineHelpOff.description: Opening sentence of a container's panel, and hover text on its state, for 'Cannot determine' when read tracing did not run on this page at all. Kept apart from containerCannotDetermineHelp, where tracing ran in part.

containerCannotDetermineHelpGpp.message: A tag in this container called the GPP consent API (__gpp). The extension did not capture a GPP string it could decode, so whether it read GPC cannot be determined.
containerCannotDetermineHelpGpp.description: Opening sentence of a container's panel, and hover text on its state, for 'Cannot determine' when the container's only possible read is a GPP call and no GPP string the extension could decode was captured. A GPP call counts as a read only when the string records a GPC value. '__gpp' is a function name: never translate it.

containerQuiet.message: Also on the page, nothing recorded: $IDS$
containerQuiet.description: Closing line of the Tag containers section: containers found on the page with nothing recorded under them (no read, no call, no cookie, no script or request). $IDS$ is a comma-separated list of container ids, never translated.

cookieNotCounted.description: In a tag container's panel, after a cookie name: the cookie is not in the count. It was written by code inside the container, and its name is not one the container's own company uses. Lowercase. Its hover text is cookieNotCountedHelp.

cookieNotCountedHelp.message: Written by code running inside this container. The name is not the container owner's own, so it is recorded and not counted.
cookieNotCountedHelp.description: Hover text on 'not counted' in a container's panel. States the rule: a cookie written inside a container is counted only when its name is one the container's own company uses; any other is recorded and charged to no company.

vdetailVendorsLoaded.description: Label in a container's panel over the companies whose scripts the container inserted, each with its category, then the domains with no company. Says only that the container loaded the script, never that it caused what the script did next.

containerAlsoScriptsFrom.description: Last line under 'Vendors loaded' in a container's panel: domains of scripts the container inserted that the classification list names no company for. $DOMAINS$ is a comma-separated list of domains, never translated.

vdetailContainersLoaded.description: Label in a container's panel over the containers whose scripts it inserted, such as a Google Tag Manager container that loads the Google tag. Not shown on the Google tag's own panel.

containerLoadedItem.description: One line under 'Tag containers loaded': the product's name, then its ids in parentheses. $NAME$ is a brand name or the Google tag's row name (containerNameGoogleTag); $IDS$ is a comma-separated list of ids, never translated.

vdetailRequestsSentTo.description: Label in a container's panel over where its tags sent requests: each company with its category and hostnames, or a domain with no company. No counts. Says only that requests were sent from inside the container, never that only its tags sent requests there.

containerRequestsTo.description: One line under 'Requests sent to': who, then the hostnames. $WHO$ is a company with its category (as vendorInCategory) or a domain; $HOSTS$ is a comma-separated list of hostnames, never translated.

vdetailScript.description: Label in a container's panel over the address of the container's own script, shown without the scheme and with the query hidden except for the id. On the Google tag's panel, one line per id.

containerCookiesPredate.message: cookies written inside containers were not recorded in this capture
containerCookiesPredate.description: Shown on a container's row in place of its cookies, when the capture was made by an older version that did not record cookies written inside containers. Something the extension did not record, so it never says 'no cookies set'. Lowercase.

listCredit.description: Credit line at the foot of the Overview, in small type, always shown: the classification list's license requires a visible credit. $LIST$ and $LICENSE$ are links whose texts are listCreditListName and listCreditLicenseName; $VERSION$ is the list's date in YYYY-MM-DD form. The full credit is in Settings, under Credits.

listCreditListName.description: Link text inside listCredit, opening the list's repository on GitHub. 'Public list' is the popup's phrase for it. 'Disconnect' is a company name and stays as it is.

listCreditLicenseName.description: Link text inside listCredit, opening the license at creativecommons.org. The license's own short name: do not translate it.

vendorGpcRead.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: a script from this vendor called the GPP consent API (__gpp), and the call returned the GPC value: the site's GPP string has the GPC field set or, with the signal off, has no GPC field, which matches the signal (vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOff). Names the mechanism. Keep the acronym 'GPP'. 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcReadHelp.message: This vendor called the GPP consent API (__gpp), and the site's GPP string has the GPC field set.
vendorGpcReadHelp.description: Hover text on the 'Read via GPP' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. '__gpp' is a function name: never translate it. 'GPC field' is the field in the GPP string.

vendorGpcReadHelpDomain.message: A script from this domain called the GPP consent API (__gpp), and the site's GPP string has the GPC field set.
vendorGpcReadHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcReadHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcReadHelp.

vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOff.message: This vendor called the GPP consent API (__gpp). The site's GPP string does not have the GPC field set, which matches your GPC signal being off on this page.
vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOff.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Read via GPP' when the GPC signal is off on this page and the site's GPP string has no GPC field set. With the signal off, the string told the vendor what was true, so the call counts as a read. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOffDomain.message: A script from this domain called the GPP consent API (__gpp). The site's GPP string does not have the GPC field set, which matches your GPC signal being off on this page.
vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOffDomain.description: vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOff on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcReadHelpSignalOff.

vendorGpcReadProperty.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: a script from this vendor read navigator.globalPrivacyControl, the property the GPC specification defines for scripts. Distinct from 'Read via GPP': a different act, measured differently (a sample of traced reads rather than an exact count of calls). 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcReadPropertyHelp.description: Hover text on the 'Read GPC property' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. 'navigator.globalPrivacyControl' is a code name: never translate it. Reads are traced on a sample, so any number of reads in the panel is a lower bound, never an exact total.

vendorGpcReadPropertyHelpDomain.message: A script from this domain read navigator.globalPrivacyControl.
vendorGpcReadPropertyHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcReadPropertyHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcReadPropertyHelp.

vendorGpcAskedNoGpcField.message: Read GPP, GPC field not set
vendorGpcAskedNoGpcField.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: this vendor called the GPP consent API, but the site's GPP string has no GPC field set, so the call returned no GPC value. The cause is in the site's string, not the vendor, so the hover text points at the GPP row. 'GPC field' is the field in the GPP string. 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcAskedNoGpcFieldHelp.message: This vendor called the GPP consent API (__gpp), but the site's GPP string does not have the GPC field set. See the GPP row above.
vendorGpcAskedNoGpcFieldHelp.description: Hover text on the 'Read GPP, GPC field not set' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. Points at the GPP row in Privacy strings, where the cause is shown.

vendorGpcAskedNoGpcFieldHelpDomain.message: A script from this domain called the GPP consent API (__gpp), but the site's GPP string does not have the GPC field set. See the GPP row above.
vendorGpcAskedNoGpcFieldHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcAskedNoGpcFieldHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcAskedNoGpcFieldHelp.

vendorGpcAskedNoResponse.message: GPP read attempted, no decodable string returned
vendorGpcAskedNoResponse.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: this vendor called the GPP consent API, and no GPP string the extension could decode was captured on this page, so what the call returned is unknown. Not the same as vendorGpcAskedNoGpcField, where a string was decoded and had no GPC field set. 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcAskedNoResponseHelp.message: This vendor called the GPP consent API (__gpp). The extension did not capture a GPP string it could decode, so whether it read GPC cannot be determined.
vendorGpcAskedNoResponseHelp.description: Hover text on the 'GPP read attempted, no decodable string returned' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. Must not say whether the call returned the GPC value: neither was observed.

vendorGpcAskedNoResponseHelpDomain.message: A script from this domain called the GPP consent API (__gpp). The extension did not capture a GPP string it could decode, so whether it read GPC cannot be determined.
vendorGpcAskedNoResponseHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcAskedNoResponseHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcAskedNoResponseHelp.

vendorGpcNotRead.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: this vendor's script ran and no read of GPC was observed from it, or from the tag container that loaded it; the hover text says which. Same words as the 'No read observed' row (labelReadNotObserved). Never claims the vendor did not read GPC by any route. 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadHelp.message: This vendor ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC.
vendorGpcNotReadHelp.description: Hover text on the 'No read observed' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. Used when the vendor's own script ran and no read was observed from it.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpDomain.message: A script from this domain ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcNotReadHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcNotReadHelp.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoader.message: This vendor ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC. Neither did $NAME$, which loaded it.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoader.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' when the script that loaded this vendor (another company's or a host's, not a container) made no read either. $NAME$ is that loader's company name or domain, never translated. It says what was observed and where; it never says this vendor read GPC or that the loader's read applied to it. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderDomain.message: A script from this domain ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC. Neither did $NAME$, which loaded it.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderDomain.description: vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoader on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoader. $NAME$ is the loader's company name or domain, never translated.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderUnchecked.message: This vendor ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC. $NAME$ loaded it; whether $NAME$ read GPC was not checked.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderUnchecked.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' when a loader is known but not every loader of this vendor could be identified, so $NAME$ was not checked for a read. $NAME$ is the loader's company name or domain, never translated. vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoader is for a loader that was checked. It says what was observed and where; it never says this vendor read GPC or that the loader's read applied to it. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderUncheckedDomai.message: A script from this domain ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC. $NAME$ loaded it; whether $NAME$ read GPC was not checked.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderUncheckedDomai.description: vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderUnchecked on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcNotReadHelpLoaderUnchecked. $NAME$ is the loader's company name or domain, never translated.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpCapped.message: The extension did not observe this vendor reading GPC, but this page exceeded the cap on traces put in place to limit the impact on page performance. You can override the cap in the extension settings to trace every read on a page.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpCapped.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' when the page went past the limit on traced GPC reads. Used in place of the loader and container variants on such a page. The last sentence points at the 'Limit GPC read tracing' setting (settingReadTraceCap). Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpCappedDomain.message: The extension did not observe a script from this domain reading GPC, but this page exceeded the cap on traces put in place to limit the impact on page performance. You can override the cap in the extension settings to trace every read on a page.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpCappedDomain.description: vendorGpcNotReadHelpCapped on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcNotReadHelpCapped.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpUnidentified.message: The extension did not observe this vendor reading GPC, but a script on this page read the GPC property and could not be identified. That read may have been this vendor's.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpUnidentified.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' on a page where a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl came from a script that could not be identified. The vendor stays under 'No read observed', because who made the read is not known. Used in place of the loader and container variants; vendorGpcNotReadHelpCapped takes precedence when both apply. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadHelpUnidentifiedDomain.message: The extension did not observe a script from this domain reading GPC, but a script on this page read the GPC property and could not be identified. That read may have been from this domain.
vendorGpcNotReadHelpUnidentifiedDomain.description: vendorGpcNotReadHelpUnidentified on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcNotReadHelpUnidentified.

vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelp.message: This vendor ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC. No tag in this page's tag container read it either.
vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelp.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' when the page runs a tag container, no container read GPC, and the vendor's own loader is not known. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpDomain.message: A script from this domain ran, and the extension did not observe it reading GPC. No tag in this page's tag container read it either.
vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelp.

vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpContaine.message: No GPC read from the tag container that loaded it ($ID$), or from any parent container.
vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpContaine.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' when the vendor's script was loaded by the tag container $ID$, and neither that container nor any container above it made a read. A tag's own read would show as a read from its container, so this states what was measured. $ID$ is a container id, never translated. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpContaine.message: No GPC read from the tag container that loaded it, or from any parent container.
vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpContaine.description: vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpContainer for a container whose address gives no id, so no id is shown.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributable.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: a read of GPC was observed that may concern this vendor (from a tag container on the page, from the script that loaded it, or through Google Consent Mode set by another container), and whether this vendor read GPC cannot be determined. The hover text says which. Same words as the 'Cannot determine' row (labelReadUndetermined). 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelp.message: The extension did not observe this vendor reading GPC. However, a tag container on this page read GPC, so whether this vendor read it cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelp.description: Hover text on the 'Cannot determine' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. Page-wide fallback when the vendor's loader cannot be resolved: whether this vendor's script ran inside the container is unknown, so it says 'a tag container on this page', never 'its container'.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpDomain.message: The extension did not observe a script from this domain reading GPC. However, a tag container on this page read GPC, so whether that script read it cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelp.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpContaine.message: The tag container that loaded this tag ($ID$) made one or more reads of GPC. Whether this tag made a read cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpContaine.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Cannot determine' when the tag container $ID$ loaded this vendor's script and a read came from that container. The tag runs inside the container, so its own read cannot be told apart from the container's; the text does not say the tag was observed not reading. 'Made one or more reads' because a read from the container can also be its own consent logic. 'This tag' is the vendor's script as the container loaded it. $ID$ is a container id, never translated.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpContaine.message: The tag container that loaded this tag made one or more reads of GPC. Whether this tag made a read cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpContaine.description: vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpContainer for a container whose address gives no id, so no id is shown.

vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRe.message: No GPC read from the tag container that loaded it ($ID$). Its parent container ($PARENT$) did read, but GPC is not passed from a parent container to a child, so tags in $ID$ must read it themselves. No such read was observed.
vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRe.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'No read observed' when the vendor's own container ($ID$) made no read but its parent container ($PARENT$) did. A child container does not receive a value its parent read, so the parent's read is context, never this tag's read. $ID$ and $PARENT$ are container ids, never translated. An ordering sentence (vendorGpcCheckOrderParentBefore or vendorGpcCheckOrderParentAfter) may follow.

vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRe.message: No GPC read from the tag container that loaded it. Its parent container ($PARENT$) did read, but GPC is not passed from a parent container to a child, so tags in it must read it themselves. No such read was observed.
vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRe.description: vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRead for a tag whose own container gives no id. $PARENT$ is the parent container's id, never translated.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpVendor.message: The extension did not observe this vendor reading GPC. However, $NAME$, which loaded it, read GPC. Whether $NAME$ passed what it read on to this vendor cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpVendor.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Cannot determine' when another company's or a host's script loaded this vendor and itself read GPC (for example, a header bidding script reading it for its bidders). $NAME$ is the loader's company name or domain, never translated. An ordering sentence may follow. It says what was observed and where; it never says this vendor read GPC or that the loader's read applied to it. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpVendorDo.message: The extension did not observe a script from this domain reading GPC. However, $NAME$, which loaded it, read GPC. Whether $NAME$ passed what it read on to that script cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpVendorDo.description: vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpVendor on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpVendor. $NAME$ is the loader's company name or domain, never translated.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpSite.message: The extension did not observe this vendor reading GPC. It was loaded by a first-party script that may have read GPC. One or more first-party scripts read GPC, but which one cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpSite.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Cannot determine' when the site's own script loaded this vendor and a read came from the site's scripts. 'First-party' means the site's own. An ordering sentence may follow. It says what was observed and where; it never says this vendor read GPC or that the loader's read applied to it. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpSiteDoma.message: The extension did not observe a script from this domain reading GPC. It was loaded by a first-party script that may have read GPC. One or more first-party scripts read GPC, but which one cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpSiteDoma.description: vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpSite on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpSite.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpConsentM.message: No GPC read from the tag container that loaded it ($ID$). However, a container this tag was not loaded through ($OTHER$) read GPC and set Google Consent Mode, which every container on the page shares. Whether this tag acts on those settings cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpConsentM.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Cannot determine' when no loader of this vendor read GPC, but another container did and set Google Consent Mode, which one page-wide store holds for every container. $ID$ is the container that loaded this tag and $OTHER$ the container that set Consent Mode; both are ids, never translated. 'Google Consent Mode' is a product name. It says what was observed and where; it never says this vendor read GPC or that the loader's read applied to it. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpConsentM.message: No GPC read from the tag container that loaded it. However, a container this tag was not loaded through ($OTHER$) read GPC and set Google Consent Mode, which every container on the page shares. Whether this tag acts on those settings cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpConsentM.description: vendorGpcCheckUnattributableHelpConsentMode for a tag whose own container gives no id. $OTHER$ is the id of the container that set Consent Mode, never translated.

vendorGpcCheckOrderBefore.message: Its first GPP call came before this tag loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderBefore.description: Sentence added after a hover text whose loader is a tag container, when the container's first GPP call came before this tag's script was inserted, so the call could have determined whether it loaded. 'Its' is the container. Based on exact call times.

vendorGpcCheckOrderAfter.message: Its first GPP call came after this tag had loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderAfter.description: As vendorGpcCheckOrderBefore, when the container's first GPP call came after this tag had loaded. The call may still affect later behavior; the sentence states only the order.

vendorGpcCheckOrderBeforeVendor.message: Its first GPP call came before this vendor loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderBeforeVendor.description: As vendorGpcCheckOrderBefore, on a company's row whose loader is another company, a host or the site. 'Its' is the loader.

vendorGpcCheckOrderAfterVendor.message: Its first GPP call came after this vendor had loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderAfterVendor.description: As vendorGpcCheckOrderAfter, on a company's row whose loader is another company, a host or the site. 'Its' is the loader.

vendorGpcCheckOrderBeforeDomain.message: Its first GPP call came before the script from this domain loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderBeforeDomain.description: As vendorGpcCheckOrderBeforeVendor, on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for.

vendorGpcCheckOrderAfterDomain.message: Its first GPP call came after the script from this domain had loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderAfterDomain.description: As vendorGpcCheckOrderAfterVendor, on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for.

vendorGpcCheckOrderParentBefore.message: The parent container's first GPP call came before this tag loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderParentBefore.description: Sentence added after vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRead when the parent container's first GPP call came before this tag loaded. Based on exact call times.

vendorGpcCheckOrderParentAfter.message: The parent container's first GPP call came after this tag had loaded.
vendorGpcCheckOrderParentAfter.description: Sentence added after vendorGpcNotReadViaContainerHelpParentRead when the parent container's first GPP call came after this tag had loaded.

vendorGpcNotApplicable.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: only passive resources (an image, a pixel, a font) loaded from this vendor, so none of its code ran and the question of a read does not apply. Not an accusation and not a gap in the capture. 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcNotApplicableHelp.message: The extension observed no script or XHR request from this vendor on this page, only resources such as pixels, images or frames.
vendorGpcNotApplicableHelp.description: Hover text on the 'No script observed' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. 'XHR' is the technical name for a script's data request; keep it or use your language's usual term.

vendorGpcNotApplicableHelpDomain.message: The extension observed no script or XHR request from this domain on this page, only resources such as pixels, images or frames.
vendorGpcNotApplicableHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcNotApplicableHelp on a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group: names the domain, never a vendor. Same rules as vendorGpcNotApplicableHelp.

vendorGpcCheckUnavailable.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column of a vendor row: the vendor is in the counts, but its individual requests were lost, so its state cannot be worked out. A limit of the capture, never a fact about the vendor. Kept distinct from 'not observable', which is used for things about the site. 'Read' means one of two acts by the vendor's own script: a call to the GPP consent API (__gpp) or a read of navigator.globalPrivacyControl. Tracing a read to a script often fails, so the state reports what was observed: word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcCheckUnavailableHelp.message: The browser paused the extension's background process and this vendor's individual requests were lost, so whether its code read GPC cannot be determined. Refresh the page to capture them again.
vendorGpcCheckUnavailableHelp.description: Hover text on the 'Not captured' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. The 'background process' is the part of the extension the browser stops when it is idle. Ends with the one action that helps.

vendorGpcCheckUnavailableHelpDomain.message: No request from this domain was recorded on this page, so whether its code ran and read GPC cannot be determined. Refresh the page to capture it again.
vendorGpcCheckUnavailableHelpDomain.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Not captured' on a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group, when the extension kept the domain's cookies but none of its requests (for example, a request made before the extension's background process restarted). Never says the domain is in the counts: nothing in that group is counted. A limit of the capture, not a fact about the domain.

vendorGpcCheckUnavailableHelpDomainCappe.message: The extension keeps a record of only so many domains without a listed company, and this page contacted more. This domain's requests came after that limit, so whether its code ran and read GPC cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUnavailableHelpDomainCappe.description: Hover text and opening panel line for 'Not captured' on a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group, when the extension had already recorded as many such domains as it keeps and left this one's requests out, keeping only its cookies. Reloading meets the same limit, so it does not suggest a reload. A limit of the extension, not a fact about the domain.

vendorGpcCheckUntraced.description: Vendor state in the 'Read GPC' column on a page where reads of the GPC property could not be observed (another extension or the browser controls the property): the vendor made no GPP call, and whether it read the property is unknown. Same words as vendorGpcCheckUnattributable; listed under the 'Cannot determine' row.

vendorGpcCheckUntracedHelp.message: GPC property reads could not be observed on this page. GPP calls were recorded and this vendor made none, but whether it read the GPC property cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUntracedHelp.description: Hover text on the 'Cannot determine' state of a company's row in the vendor list, and the opening line of its expanded panel. Word it as an observation, never an accusation. Used for vendorGpcCheckUntraced.

vendorGpcCheckUntracedHelpDomain.message: GPC property reads could not be observed on this page. GPP calls were recorded and no script from this domain made one, but whether a script from this domain read the GPC property cannot be determined.
vendorGpcCheckUntracedHelpDomain.description: vendorGpcCheckUntracedHelp on a row for a domain the vendor list names no company for: 'this vendor' becomes 'a script from this domain'. Same rules as vendorGpcCheckUntracedHelp.

vendorGpcUnlistedDomain.description: State in the 'Read GPC' column for a row that is a domain rather than a company: the vendor list puts the domain in a counted category but names no company for it, so there is no vendor to judge. Not a capture loss ('Not captured') and not a fact about anyone's behavior. Word it as an observation, never an accusation.

vendorGpcUnlistedDomainHelp.message: The vendor list does not name a company for this domain.
vendorGpcUnlistedDomainHelp.description: Opening line of the panel for a 'No company listed' row. Says why the panel is nearly empty. Does not name the list's provider: only the credit line and Settings, Credits name it.

vendorUspChecked.description: Secondary line on a vendor row, shown only when this vendor's script called the US Privacy API (__uspapi) and the page's __uspapi answered with a value. $STATE$ is the decoded phrase the page's US Privacy row also uses, such as 'Opted out of sale: N'. Keep 'USP'.

vendorTcfChecked.description: Secondary line on a vendor row, shown only when this vendor's script asked the TCF API (__tcfapi) for consent data and at least one purpose is granted. $RATIO$ is 'granted/total', such as 3/10. Keep 'TCF'. vendorTcfNoPurposes and vendorTcfNoneGranted cover the other cases.

vendorTcfNoPurposes.description: Secondary line on a vendor row in place of vendorTcfChecked when the TCF string lists no purposes, so '0/0' is never shown.

vendorTcfNoneGranted.description: Secondary line on a vendor row in place of vendorTcfChecked when purposes are listed and none is granted.

vendorLoadedViaGtm.description: The vendor's script was inserted by a Google Tag Manager container. $ID$ is its id, such as GTM-ABC12. 'Google Tag Manager' is a product name. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaGoogleTag.description: Inserted by the Google tag (gtag.js), not a container. $ID$ is its measurement or conversion id, such as G-ABC or AW-123. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaManager.description: Inserted by another tag management product. $MANAGER$ is its brand name (such as Tealium, Adobe Launch or Segment) and $ID$ its container or property id. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaTagManager.description: Inserted by a tag container whose id could not be read from its address. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaContainers.description: Two or more containers each inserted one of this vendor's scripts. $IDS$ is a comma-separated list of their ids. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaParent.description: Added after a container fragment when that container was itself inserted by another container. $PARENT$ is the parent's id. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaVendor.description: Inserted by another company's script (such as a header bidding script loading a bidder, or a consent manager releasing a script it held back). $NAME$ is that company's name from the classification list. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedViaHost.description: Inserted by a third-party script whose domain the classification list does not name. $DOMAIN$ is its domain. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedBySite.description: The vendor's script was in the page's HTML, or inserted by the site's own script. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedBySiteScript.message: loaded by a site script that also loads $COUNT$ other vendors
vendorLoadedBySiteScript.description: Inserted by a site script file that inserted other vendors' scripts too. $COUNT$ is how many others, two or more. Singular: vendorLoadedBySiteScriptOne. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedBySiteScriptOne.message: loaded by a site script that also loads 1 other vendor
vendorLoadedBySiteScriptOne.description: vendorLoadedBySiteScript when there is exactly one other vendor. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedAlsoBySite.description: Added after the main loader when some of the vendor's scripts were also inserted by the site itself. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorLoadedAlsoByVendor.description: Added after the main loader when some of the vendor's scripts were also inserted by another company or host. $NAME$ is that company name or domain. Loaded-by line under a vendor row and on the Requests tab: who inserted the vendor's script, from the page's own records. Several fragments are joined with commas. Identifiers (container ids, company names, domains) are never translated. Shown only when the records could tell; never says 'not through a container'.

vendorsNoneSeen.description: Shown in place of the vendor list when no vendor was observed on the page. Must read differently from stateNoAdTech, which explains the missing count higher on the same screen: this one describes the list.

stateNoAdTech.message: No third-party advertising or analytics domains were detected.
stateNoAdTech.description: Shown in place of the cookie count when no third-party advertising or analytics domain was contacted. States what was not found, never that the site behaved well. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' are category names from the classification list. Keep it short: a dash already stands in for the number above it.

stateIneligible.message: The extension cannot inspect this page.
stateIneligible.description: The one notice on the Overview, with nothing else shown, on a page the extension cannot inspect: the browser's own pages (settings, extensions, history), other extensions' pages, the browser's extension store, and local files. The store is an https page, so the sentence must not say what kind of address can be inspected. Must not suggest reloading, which never makes such a page inspectable. Not shown on a new tab, which has stateNewTab.

stateNewTab.message: Open a site in this tab to inspect it.
stateNewTab.description: The one notice on the Overview, with nothing else shown, when the tab holds the browser's new tab page or a blank page: there is nothing in it to inspect yet. Says what to do, not what is wrong. Must not suggest reloading, which never helps here. 'Site' is the one word the extension uses for what the reader visits, never 'website'.

stateNeedsReload.message: The extension doesn't have information about this page. Reload the page to inspect it.
stateNeedsReload.description: The one notice at the top of the Overview, with the results hidden, when the extension did not observe the page load: the tab was already open when the extension was installed, updated or turned back on, or the browser restored the page from its back/forward cache, where the load happened under an earlier capture. States that nothing is known, then the one action that fixes it. Must not describe the page.

stateLoadFailed.message: This page did not load, so there was nothing on it to observe. Reload the page to try again.
stateLoadFailed.description: The one notice at the top of the Overview, with the results hidden, when the page failed to load and the browser showed its own error page (no network, an address that does not resolve, a certificate error, a page another extension blocked). States the cause and the one action that helps. Must not say why the page failed, which the browser's page already says, and must not describe the site.

stateNoData.message: Nothing was received for this page. Reload the page, or reopen this panel.
stateNoData.description: Shown in place of the results when the popup or side panel asked the extension's background process for this tab and got nothing back. Not shown while a page is still loading (statePending). Both actions make the panel ask again. 'Panel' covers both the toolbar popup and the side panel.

stateIncomplete.message: Part of this page was not observed. Refresh the page to inspect it again.
stateIncomplete.description: Overview notice for a capture marked incomplete with no recorded reason, which only captures from older versions have. Newer captures name a reason, and each has its own notice (stateSaveFailed, stateDeliveryGap, stateConsentCallsCapped, or requestsDropped on the Requests tab).

stateSaveFailed.message: Some captured data could not be saved, so counts may be incomplete. Refresh the page to inspect it again.
