stateSaveFailed.description: Overview notice when part of the capture could not be saved or read back, so the counts may be behind what the page did. Also shown when the page was prerendered (loaded by the browser before it was shown) and part of what it did then was not kept. The only notice that says the counts may be incomplete. Outranks the other incomplete notices; only one is shown.

stateDeliveryGap.message: Some data from the page did not reach the extension, so some counts and checks may be missing. Refresh the page to inspect it again.
stateDeliveryGap.description: Overview notice when things the page did (consent API calls, reads of the GPC property, cookies written by scripts) were observed in the page but never reached the extension's background process. Request counts are unaffected; cookie counts can be affected.

stateConsentCallsCapped.message: This page made more consent API calls than the extension supports, so some vendor checks may be missing.
stateConsentCallsCapped.description: Overview notice when the page made more distinct consent API calls than the extension records (200 per tab). A vendor whose read was one of the calls left out can show as not having read GPC. 'Consent API calls' matches the vendor panel's label (vdetailConsentCalls).

requestsDropped.message: Some requests were dropped while the extension was idle. Refresh the page to capture the full list.
requestsDropped.description: Line above the list on the Requests tab when the browser stopped the extension's idle background process and the request list was lost with it. The counts and the Overview are unaffected, so this is the only place it is said.

requestsDroppedCookiesKept.message: The extension was idle and dropped this page's requests. The ones that set a cookie are still listed. Refresh the page to capture the full list.
requestsDroppedCookiesKept.description: In place of requestsDropped when the extension kept every request that set a cookie: those are listed, and requests that set nothing are gone. The Overview's counts are unaffected. A limit of the capture, not a fact about the site.

requestsDroppedSomeCookiesKept.message: The extension was idle and dropped this page's requests. Some of the ones that set a cookie are still listed. Refresh the page to capture the full list.
requestsDroppedSomeCookiesKept.description: In place of requestsDroppedCookiesKept when not every request that set a cookie could be kept (the extension keeps up to 2,000 a page, fewer when its storage runs short). The Overview's counts are unaffected.

btnLooksWrong.description: Button at the foot of the popup. Opens the finding report, whose title repeats it (reportTitleFinding). Asks for anything that looks wrong, not only what the reader is sure of. Should feel safe to press: a preview comes before anything opens.

btnSettings.description: Icon button in the popup's header that opens Settings: its accessible name.

btnOpenPanel.description: Icon button in the popup's header, beside Settings: its accessible name and its hover text. Opens the same page in the browser's side panel, which stays open while the reader browses. 'Side panel' is the browser's own name for that area; use the name the browser's menus use in the target language.

btnBack.description: Icon button that returns from Settings or a report screen to the results: its accessible name.

groupSignal.description: Settings group heading over the setting that sends the signal.

settingSendSignal.message: Send GPC when nothing else does
settingSendSignal.description: Settings switch label: send the GPC signal only when nothing else (the browser or another extension) already sends it.

settingSendSignalDesc.message: Adds the Sec-GPC header to requests and sets the navigator.globalPrivacyControl page property, if nothing else has already. Turning this off never disables a signal set by the browser or another extension.
settingSendSignalDesc.description: Line under the send switch. Names both ways the signal is sent: the Sec-GPC request header and the navigator.globalPrivacyControl property that page scripts read. Both are code names: never translate them.

settingSendSignalNative.message: The browser is sending this signal. Manage it in your browser settings.
settingSendSignalNative.description: Replaces settingSendSignalDesc when the browser itself sends the signal, which leaves the switch with no effect.

settingSendSignalNativeOff.message: Your browser supports this signal and has it off. Turn it on in your browser settings.
settingSendSignalNativeOff.description: Replaces settingSendSignalDesc when the browser supports GPC and has it off. The switch still works: it controls this extension's own Sec-GPC header.

groupObservation.description: Settings group heading over the observation settings.

settingObserve.description: Settings switch label for inspecting pages as the user browses. Not currently shown.

settingObserveDesc.message: Reads pages you visit. All information stays on your device.
settingObserveDesc.description: Line under the settingObserve switch: what the extension reads stays on the device. Not currently shown.

settingBadge.description: Settings switch label: whether the cookie count appears on the toolbar icon.

groupAbout.description: Settings group heading over the version, source code, license and known limitations rows, and the statement that limits reliance on the extension.

linkRepo.description: Link text to the source code repository, beside the 'Source code' label (aboutLinks). Names the destination, so it differs from the label. 'GitHub' is a product name. Keep the arrow.

aboutLicense.description: Settings, About group: label of the row that names the license of this extension's own code.

aboutLicenseDesc.description: Under 'License'. $LICENSE$ is the license identifier of the extension's own code and $COPYRIGHT$ its copyright line; both are filled in by the code and never translated. The bundled data has its own licenses, credited in the Credits group.

aboutNoWarranty.message: This program comes with ABSOLUTELY NO WARRANTY. See the license for details.
aboutNoWarranty.description: Under 'License', after the license name. The GPL's own no-warranty notice for an interactive program; the capitals are the license's and stay. 'The license' is the link beside the row.

linkCodeLicense.description: Link beside the 'License' row in About, to the text of the GNU General Public License, version 3. Same words as the Credits group's license links.

statementObserved.message: GPC Inspector records what was observed on a page load. It is not legal advice.
statementObserved.description: First paragraph of the statement that limits reliance on the extension. 'GPC Inspector' is the product name. The same three paragraphs close Settings (About), the saved summary and the README: keep the wording identical in each place.

statementFinding.message: A finding is an observation, not a legal conclusion. A page with no findings may still share data in ways the extension cannot see.
statementFinding.description: Second paragraph of the statement that limits reliance on the extension. 'Finding' is the product's word for what the popup reports. The same three paragraphs close Settings (About), the saved summary and the README: keep the wording identical in each place.

statementIndependent.message: GPC Inspector is independent and is not affiliated with the Global Privacy Control project, Disconnect, or any regulator.
statementIndependent.description: Third paragraph of the statement that limits reliance on the extension. 'Global Privacy Control' is the standard's proper name and Disconnect the list's maintainer: keep both as written. The same three paragraphs close Settings (About), the saved summary and the README: keep the wording identical in each place.

firstRunTitle.description: Title of the one-time welcome screen, shown before first use to new users and to users updating from an earlier version alike. Must be true for both.

firstRunSignalOn.message: Your GPC signal is currently on. You can turn it off in Settings.
firstRunSignalOn.description: Shown under the welcome title only to users updating from an earlier version, when this extension is sending the signal. Those users installed a switch, so the first thing they read is its state.

firstRunSignalOff.message: Your GPC signal is currently off. You can turn it on in Settings.
firstRunSignalOff.description: As firstRunSignalOn, when sending is off.

firstRunSignalNative.message: Your browser supports sending the GPC signal. You can turn it on or off in your browser settings.
firstRunSignalNative.description: As firstRunSignalOn, when the browser itself sets the signal. The extension's own switch has no effect then, so this points at the browser's setting.

firstRunSignalNativeOff.message: Your browser supports this signal and has it off. Turn it on in your browser settings.
firstRunSignalNativeOff.description: As firstRunSignalNative, when the browser supports GPC and has it off.

firstRunWhy.message: The Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal asks each site you visit not to sell or share your data. Instead of turning it on and hoping the site did the right thing, we built GPC Inspector so you can see exactly what each site did with your opt-out signal.
firstRunWhy.description: First paragraph of the welcome screen: why the extension exists. The standard's full name appears once, with its abbreviation; keep both. 'GPC Inspector' is the product name. 'We' are the makers of the extension.

firstRunBody.message: On every page, you can see whether the signal was sent, which scripts read it, what the site's privacy strings tell third parties about your choice, and which advertising or analytics domains set cookies while it was on. If nothing else sends the signal, we can send it for you.
firstRunBody.description: Second paragraph of the welcome screen: what the reader can see on every page, then that the extension can send the signal, a setting the reader can turn off. 'Privacy strings' names the popup section (sectionPrivacyStrings). 'While it was on' matches the cookie count's caption.

firstRunPromise.message: Everything this extension observes stays on your device. Nothing is shared with us or anyone else. We do make one extra request for the current site's /.well-known/gpc.json file, which states whether it supports the GPC signal. You can turn this off in Settings.
firstRunPromise.description: Third paragraph of the welcome screen: the privacy promise and, straight after it, the one network request that qualifies it. That request must stay in this paragraph: it is the only one the extension makes. '/.well-known/gpc.json' is a fixed path: never translate it.

firstRunAsk.message: There is one area where we need your help: if you find a site where what we report doesn't look right, please let us know with the "Finding looks wrong" button at the bottom of the popup. It shows you what the report includes, then opens a prefilled GitHub issue you can check before submitting.
firstRunAsk.description: Fourth paragraph of the welcome screen: asks for reports of wrong results. Quotes the button label btnLooksWrong, so use the same translation as that key. The last sentence keeps the promise above true: the reader sees what the report includes and sends it, not the extension.

firstRunAccept.description: Button that closes the welcome screen.

countCookiesOff.message: third-party cookies set by advertising or analytics domains with your GPC signal off
countCookiesOff.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal off. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Plural. The baseline a reader compares with by turning the signal on and reloading; the two counts are never added. Used when no counted cookie belongs to a named vendor; otherwise a countCookiesOffBy caption is used. 'Third-party' is stated so that the first-party line below it (countFirstPartyVendor) reads as a different measure. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesOffOne.message: third-party cookie set by an advertising or analytics domain with your GPC signal off
countCookiesOffOne.description: Singular of countCookiesOff: the count above is 1. Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal off. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. 'Third-party' is stated so that the first-party line below it (countFirstPartyVendor) reads as a different measure. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesOffZero.message: No third-party cookies set by advertising or analytics vendors with your GPC signal off
countCookiesOffZero.description: Headline when no counted cookie was set with the GPC signal off. A full sentence with no number. Also shown when advertising or analytics domains were contacted and set no counted cookie, so it must not read as 'no vendors were present'. The baseline a reader compares with by turning the signal on and reloading; the two counts are never added. 'Third-party' is stated so that the first-party line below it (countFirstPartyVendor) reads as a different measure. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesByVendors.message: third-party cookies set by $VENDORS$ advertising and analytics vendors while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesByVendors.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. This form: several cookies, several vendors. $VENDORS$ is the number of vendors. Used only for an older capture that does not record each vendor's category; otherwise a caption naming each category is used (countCookiesByBoth and the forms beside it). 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesByOneVendor.message: third-party cookies set by 1 advertising or analytics vendor while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesByOneVendor.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. This form: several cookies, one vendor. Used only for an older capture that does not record each vendor's category; otherwise a caption naming each category is used (countCookiesByBoth and the forms beside it). 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesOneByVendor.message: third-party cookie set by 1 advertising or analytics vendor while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesOneByVendor.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. This form: one cookie, so one vendor. Used only for an older capture that does not record each vendor's category; otherwise a caption naming each category is used (countCookiesByBoth and the forms beside it). 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names.

countCookiesByBoth.message: third-party cookies set by $ADVERTISING$ advertising and $ANALYTICS$ analytics vendors while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesByBoth.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Counts the vendors that set a counted cookie, by category: a vendor is a company, and the category is the one the classification list gives the domain the cookie came from. A company with cookies from both categories is counted once in each. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names. This form: vendors of both categories, two or more of them analytics. $ADVERTISING$ and $ANALYTICS$ are the vendor counts; $ADVERTISING$ may be 1, since 'vendors' follows the last number.

countCookiesByBothOneAnalytics.message: third-party cookies set by $ADVERTISING$ advertising and 1 analytics vendor while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesByBothOneAnalytics.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Counts the vendors that set a counted cookie, by category: a vendor is a company, and the category is the one the classification list gives the domain the cookie came from. A company with cookies from both categories is counted once in each. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names. This form: vendors of both categories, exactly one of them analytics, so the sentence ends on 'vendor'. $ADVERTISING$ is the advertising vendor count.

countCookiesByAdvertising.message: third-party cookies set by $VENDORS$ advertising vendors while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesByAdvertising.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Counts the vendors that set a counted cookie, by category: a vendor is a company, and the category is the one the classification list gives the domain the cookie came from. A company with cookies from both categories is counted once in each. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names. This form: two or more vendors, all advertising. $VENDORS$ is the vendor count.

countCookiesByOneAdvertising.message: third-party cookies set by 1 advertising vendor while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesByOneAdvertising.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Counts the vendors that set a counted cookie, by category: a vendor is a company, and the category is the one the classification list gives the domain the cookie came from. A company with cookies from both categories is counted once in each. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names. This form: several cookies, one advertising vendor.

countCookiesOneByAdvertising.message: third-party cookie set by 1 advertising vendor while your GPC signal was on
countCookiesOneByAdvertising.description: Headline caption under the large cookie count, with the GPC signal on. It continues the number above it, so it carries no cookie number of its own. Counts the vendors that set a counted cookie, by category: a vendor is a company, and the category is the one the classification list gives the domain the cookie came from. A company with cookies from both categories is counted once in each. 'Advertising' and 'analytics' name the category the classification list gives the domain that set the cookie, not what the cookie is used for: translate them as category names. This form: one cookie, so one vendor, advertising.

countCookiesByAnalytics.message: third-party cookies set by $VENDORS$ analytics vendors while your GPC signal was on

statePending.description: Shown in place of the results while the page is still loading and observations are still arriving.

sourceUnknown.description: Tag after the signal status line when the extension's background process did not answer. Not the same as 'off' and not the same as 'still loading' (statePending): do not merge these. Lowercase; it continues the line.

actionTitleSending.description: Hover title of the toolbar icon when it is blue, before a page has reported anything: the default on every tab, and what stays on pages the extension cannot observe (browser pages, the store). Reflects this extension's own setting, so it names no page; actionTitleOn replaces it once the page reports the signal was set. Must not claim protection. 'GPC Inspector' is the product name.

actionTitleOn.message: GPC Inspector: GPC signal set on this page
actionTitleOn.description: Hover title of the toolbar icon when it is blue, on a tab whose page has reported: the signal was set as this page loaded (the property read true, or the page's request carried Sec-GPC). Says what was set, not who set it; the popup's status line says who. Must not claim protection: the icon reports a signal and blocks nothing.

actionTitleOff.message: GPC Inspector: no GPC signal on this page
actionTitleOff.description: Hover title of the toolbar icon when it is gray: nothing set the signal as this page loaded (not the browser, not this extension, not another one). Also the default on pages the extension cannot observe, where it reflects this extension's own setting.

actionTitleRuleFailed.message: GPC Inspector: cannot set the signal in this browser version
actionTitleRuleFailed.description: Hover title of the toolbar icon, shown with a ! badge, when sending is on but the browser did not install the rule that adds the Sec-GPC header. Says what failed; must not suggest the signal is being sent.

findingGppConflict.message: The site's GPP string has the GPC field set and records that you did not opt out of sale, sharing or targeted advertising. IAB guidance considers this combination conflicting.
findingGppConflict.description: Finding notice above the results. The site's GPP string has the GPC field set to 1 (its consent manager recorded the GPC signal) and an opt-out field of 2 (did not opt out). IAB guidance calls that pair conflicting. Never 'detected': the field is something the site set, not something the extension detected. 'GPC field' is the field in the GPP string.

findingGpcGppMismatch.message: The GPC signal and the GPC field in the site's GPP string do not match.
findingGpcGppMismatch.description: Neutral notice above the results, used for both directions of the mismatch: the signal was set and the string's GPC field says no, or the signal was not set and the field says yes. The two values follow below as label and value pairs (labelGpcSignalValue, labelGppGpcFieldValue): do not fold them into this sentence, and do not add a cause, since several innocent causes exist and the extension cannot tell them apart.

labelGpcSignalValue.description: Left column of the mismatch pair under findingGpcGppMismatch: what this browser did. Same words as the popup's first line.

valueGpcSignalSet.description: Right column of the mismatch pair when the signal was set. Names both ways a consent manager can see it: the property was set and the header was sent. $COUNT$ is the number of observed requests that carried Sec-GPC.

valueGpcSignalNotSet.description: Right column of the mismatch pair when the signal was not set. Same words as the status line for that state.

labelGppGpcFieldValue.description: Left column of the mismatch pair: the GPC field in the site's GPP string. Uses the same 'GPC field' as valueGpcFieldYes and valueGpcFieldNo. Keep the acronyms.

valueGppGpcFieldSet.description: Right column of the mismatch pair: the string's GPC field is 1. Says 'set' to match the GPC signal value above it, since the notice compares the two. The number in parentheses is the raw IAB value: translate the word, keep the number.

valueGppGpcFieldNotSet.description: Right column of the mismatch pair: the string's GPC field is 0. Same wording as valueGpcSignalNotSet, for the same reason as valueGppGpcFieldSet. Translate the words, keep the number.

gppNoteMismatchSignalSet.message: Does not match the GPC signal, which this browser set on this visit.
gppNoteMismatchSignalSet.description: Note at the top of the expanded GPP row, shown only when the string's GPC field is 0 while the signal was set. Short, because the notice above the results states the mismatch in full.

gppNoteMismatchSignalNotSet.message: Does not match the GPC signal, which this browser did not set on this visit.
gppNoteMismatchSignalNotSet.description: Note at the top of the expanded GPP row, shown only when the string's GPC field is 1 while the signal was not set. Gives no cause: it is often a string kept from an earlier visit, but the extension cannot tell.

lineGppWirePlaceholder.message: A request to $HOST$ carried an unfilled placeholder instead of a GPP string:
lineGppWirePlaceholder.description: Line in the expanded GPP row: a gpp= parameter on an outbound request held a template placeholder the ad tag never filled in, such as [GPP]. The value follows in code type. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated; a hover lists the others. Not a disagreement with the page: it was never a string. Ends with a colon because the value follows.

lineGppWireInvalid.message: A request to $HOST$ carried a value that is not a GPP string:
lineGppWireInvalid.description: Line in the expanded GPP row: a gpp= parameter on an outbound request was neither a GPP string nor a placeholder. The value follows in code type. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated.

lineUspWirePlaceholder.message: A request to $HOST$ carried an unfilled placeholder instead of a US Privacy string:
lineUspWirePlaceholder.description: Line in the expanded US Privacy row. As lineGppWirePlaceholder, for the us_privacy= parameter. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated.

lineUspWireInvalid.message: A request to $HOST$ carried a value that is not a US Privacy string:
lineUspWireInvalid.description: Line in the expanded US Privacy row. As lineGppWireInvalid, for the us_privacy= parameter. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated.

lineGppWireDiffers.message: A request to $HOST$ carried a different GPP string:
lineGppWireDiffers.description: Line in the expanded GPP row: a valid GPP string on an outbound request that differs from the one the page reported, one line per distinct string. The string follows in code type. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated; a hover lists the others. The notice above the results names one of these; this lists each.

lineGppWireCarried.message: A request to $HOST$ carried a GPP string:
lineGppWireCarried.description: Line in the expanded GPP row when the page reported no GPP string: one line per distinct string that requests carried in gpp=. The string follows in code type. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated; a hover lists the others.

lineUspCookieDiffers.message: The page's usprivacy cookie holds a different US Privacy string:
lineUspCookieDiffers.description: Line in the expanded US Privacy row: the site's usprivacy cookie holds a different string from the one the page's US Privacy API (__uspapi) reports, which is the one the row decodes. The cookie's string follows in code type. 'usprivacy' is a cookie name: never translate it.

lineUspWireDiffers.message: A request to $HOST$ carried a different US Privacy string:
lineUspWireDiffers.description: Line in the expanded US Privacy row. As lineGppWireDiffers, for the us_privacy= parameter. Compared with the string the row decodes: the page's, or, where the page reported none, the first one a request carried. $HOST$ is the first host it was sent to, never translated.

valueUspWireOnly.description: US Privacy row value when the page reported no string (no __uspapi answer, no usprivacy cookie) and only an outbound request carried one. The decoded fields are that request's string, not the site's. Same words as valueGppWireOnly.

lineUspWireOnly.message: No US Privacy string was provided by __uspapi or the usprivacy cookie. A request to $HOST$ carried the one shown here.
lineUspWireOnly.description: First line of the expanded US Privacy row when the row shows valueUspWireOnly and __uspapi was watched. Says whose string the decoded fields are. $HOST$ is the host, never translated. '__uspapi' and 'usprivacy' are code names: never translate them.

lineUspWireOnlyUnwatched.message: __uspapi could not be watched on this page, and the usprivacy cookie held no string. A request to $HOST$ carried the one shown here.
lineUspWireOnlyUnwatched.description: lineUspWireOnly when the extension could not watch __uspapi, so the page may have answered unseen. Says that, rather than claiming the page provided no string. $HOST$ is the host, never translated.

findingGppDisagreeHost.message: The GPP string reported by the page ($PAGE$) is different from what a request to $HOST$ carried ($WIRE$).
findingGppDisagreeHost.description: Finding notice: the GPP string the page reported differs from one an outbound request carried. $PAGE$ and $WIRE$ are the two strings and $HOST$ the host the request went to; none is translated.

findingUspDisagreeHost.message: The US Privacy string reported by the page ($PAGE$) is different from what a request to $HOST$ carried ($WIRE$).
findingUspDisagreeHost.description: Finding notice: the US Privacy string the page reported differs from one an outbound request carried. $PAGE$ and $WIRE$ are the two strings and $HOST$ the host the request went to; none is translated.

findingGppDisagree.message: The GPP string reported by the page ($PAGE$) is different from what at least one outbound request carried ($WIRE$).
findingGppDisagree.description: As findingGppDisagreeHost, for an older capture that did not record which host the request went to. $PAGE$ and $WIRE$ are the two strings, never translated.

findingDeclaredHonorButSet.message: This site publishes /.well-known/gpc.json with gpc set to true. Cookies were set by third-party domains categorized as advertising or analytics.
findingDeclaredHonorButSet.description: Finding notice. States two facts from the site itself (its published /.well-known/gpc.json file and its own responses) and leaves the conclusion to the reader: setting a cookie is not by itself a sale or a share. 'Categorized' credits the category to the classification list, which this text does not name. '/.well-known/gpc.json' is a fixed path, and 'gpc' and 'true' are the file's own words: never translate them.

findingUspCookieDisagree.message: The US Privacy string reported by the page ($PAGE$) is different from the one in its usprivacy cookie ($COOKIE$).
findingUspCookieDisagree.description: Finding notice: the page's two US Privacy sources disagree, the US Privacy API (__uspapi) and the site's usprivacy cookie. Shown in place of findingUspDisagreeHost when every request carried what __uspapi reports. $PAGE$ and $COOKIE$ are the two strings, never translated.

findingUspRequestsDisagree.message: Requests did not agree on the US Privacy string: $VALUE1$ to $HOST1$, $VALUE2$ to $HOST2$.
findingUspRequestsDisagree.description: Finding notice when the page reported no US Privacy string and requests carried different ones. A claim about what was sent to partners, not about the page. $VALUE1$ and $VALUE2$ are the first two strings and $HOST1$ and $HOST2$ the first host each was sent to; none is translated. The expanded US Privacy row lists every one.

findingGppRequestsDisagree.message: Requests did not agree on the GPP string: $VALUE1$ to $HOST1$, $VALUE2$ to $HOST2$.
findingGppRequestsDisagree.description: As findingUspRequestsDisagree, for GPP: the page reported no GPP string, and requests carried different ones in their gpp= parameter. $VALUE1$ and $VALUE2$ are the strings and $HOST1$ and $HOST2$ the hosts; none is translated.

findingConfirmationShownButSet.message: This page showed a GPC confirmation notice. Cookies were set by third-party domains categorized as advertising or analytics.
findingConfirmationShownButSet.description: Finding notice, the same finding as findingDeclaredHonorButSet when the site's statement is a notice on the page rather than its published file. Uses the words of the row 'GPC confirmation shown on page' (labelConfirmation) so the two read as one fact. Does not quote or paraphrase the site's notice. States two facts and leaves the conclusion to the reader.

findingDeclaredAndShownButSet.message: This site publishes /.well-known/gpc.json with gpc set to true, and this page showed a GPC confirmation notice. Cookies were set by third-party domains categorized as advertising or analytics.
findingDeclaredAndShownButSet.description: Finding notice when the site made both statements: its published file declares GPC support and the page showed a confirmation notice. One notice, since it is one finding. Same rules as findingDeclaredHonorButSet.

findingUspDisagree.message: The US Privacy string reported by the page ($PAGE$) is different from what at least one outbound request carried ($WIRE$).
findingUspDisagree.description: As findingUspDisagreeHost, for an older capture that did not record which host the request went to. The page's string comes from __uspapi, or the usprivacy cookie when that is absent; the other is the us_privacy= parameter of the most recent request that carried one. $PAGE$ and $WIRE$ are the two strings, never translated.

countFirstPartyVendor.message: Also $COUNT$ first-party cookies written by advertising or analytics scripts
countFirstPartyVendor.description: Supporting line under the headline count: $COUNT$ distinct first-party cookies (on the site's own domain) written by a script served from an advertising or analytics domain. The headline counts third-party cookies; this is a different fact and is never added to it. Shown only with the signal on. 'First-party' matches the Requests tab's party labels. Singular: countFirstPartyVendorOne.

valueNotObservable.description: Value: the extension could not look. A fact about the extension, not the site, and must not read as an absence. Keep distinct from 'not present' and 'none observed'.

valueNoneObserved.description: Value: the extension looked and found nothing. Keep distinct from 'not observable' (could not look at all). Used in vendor panel sections such as consent API calls, which are watched for the whole page.

noticeSameOwnerAdvertising.message: $OWNER$ is listed as the owner of this site and is categorized as a third-party advertising vendor. Its other domains will continue to be categorized as a third-party advertising vendor.
noticeSameOwnerAdvertising.description: Neutral notice above the count when the company the classification list names as this site's owner is also one of the page's vendors. $OWNER$ is that company's name, never translated. 'Categorized' credits the category to the list, which this text does not name. This form: every domain of that company seen on the page is in Advertising. Other forms: noticeSameOwnerAnalytics, noticeSameOwnerBoth.

noticeSameOwnerAnalytics.message: $OWNER$ is listed as the owner of this site and is categorized as a third-party analytics vendor. Its other domains will continue to be categorized as a third-party analytics vendor.
noticeSameOwnerAnalytics.description: Neutral notice above the count when the company the classification list names as this site's owner is also one of the page's vendors. $OWNER$ is that company's name, never translated. 'Categorized' credits the category to the list, which this text does not name. This form: every domain of that company seen on the page is in Analytics.

noticeSameOwnerBoth.message: $OWNER$ is listed as the owner of this site and is categorized as a third-party advertising and analytics vendor. Its other domains will continue to be categorized as a third-party advertising and analytics vendor.
noticeSameOwnerBoth.description: Neutral notice above the count when the company the classification list names as this site's owner is also one of the page's vendors. $OWNER$ is that company's name, never translated. 'Categorized' credits the category to the list, which this text does not name. This form: that company has domains on the page in both Advertising and Analytics.

stateCaptureUnavailable.description: Notice when part of the page could not be inspected. $WHAT$ is a plain-language list such as 'the GPP privacy string or Consent Mode'. States the fact, not a cause: never 'blocked', since the extension usually cannot tell what took control of the property first.

btnCopy.description: Button on the Requests tab. Copies the visible rows as plain text. Short; sits in a toolbar.

reqFilterAll.description: Requests filter: every request. Lower case; reads as a chip label, followed by a count.

reqFilterThirdParty.description: Requests filter: requests to a domain other than the site being visited. Lowercase, like the other filters; followed by a count.

reqFilterSetCookie.description: Requests filter: responses that set a cookie. Keep the HTTP header name as-is.

reqFilterUncategorized.description: Requests filter: third-party domains the classification list gives no category, including domains it names an owner for and nothing else. First-party requests are never in it. Also the label on a Requests row with no company and no category. Same word as the vendor list's group heading (categoryUncategorized). Lowercase, like the other filters.

reqNoneMatch.description: Shown when a filter selects nothing.

reqNoneCaptured.message: No requests captured for this page yet.
reqNoneCaptured.description: Shown when nothing has been observed at all.

reqCopied.description: Brief confirmation after the Copy button is pressed.

reqRedirect.description: Marker on a request row: this response was a redirect hop, which can set its own cookies.

reqNoGpc.description: Marker on a request row that did not carry the Sec-GPC header. Only these exceptions are marked, since nearly every request carries it. The header is named in the expanded detail (detailSecGpc).

reqNoGpcProperty.description: Marker on a collapsed row for a cookie a page script wrote while navigator.globalPrivacyControl was not true. A script write has no request, so no header was or was not sent; the property is what the script could have read. Used in place of reqNoGpc on these rows.

reqScriptWriteMeta.description: On the second line of a collapsed row for a cookie a page script wrote, in place of a request's status code and resource type: such a row is not an HTTP request. The vendor or party follows after a separator. Lowercase.

reqScriptWritesNote.message: Also $COUNT$ cookies written by page scripts, listed with the requests.
reqScriptWritesNote.description: Line above the request list when it includes cookies that page scripts wrote. Every number on the tab counts HTTP requests only; these rows are listed with them and counted here, once. $COUNT$ is the number of writes listed, not of distinct cookies. Singular: reqScriptWritesNoteOne.

reqScriptWritesNoteOne.message: Also 1 cookie written by a page script, listed with the requests.
reqScriptWritesNoteOne.description: Singular of reqScriptWritesNote: the list holds one cookie a page script wrote.

vdetailNetwork.description: Heading in the expanded vendor panel, over the request counts.

vdetailSigned.description: Follows a count like '12/14'. Reads as '12/14 requests carried your signal'.

vdetailResourceTypes.description: Label in the expanded vendor panel for the kinds of request seen from this vendor. Always shown; an empty value reads 'not observable', never 'none'. This row is the evidence behind the 'No script observed' state.

hintResourceTypes.message: The browser's own name for what each request was for. "other" is the browser's catch-all for requests that fit none of its categories, such as beacons and some background fetches.
hintResourceTypes.description: Hover text on the 'Resource types' label in the expanded vendor panel. The values come straight from the browser and are not renamed. Keep the quoted value 'other' untranslated: it is the literal value shown.

vdetailCookies.description: Heading in the expanded vendor panel, over the cookie list.

vdetailCookieUnsigned.description: Last attribute on a cookie's line in a vendor panel: the cookie was set on a request that did not carry the GPC signal while the signal was on. The row above lists only cookies set on requests that carried it, so this says why the name is in the panel. Also after a name in the First party panel's lists, in parentheses. A fact about the request, not a judgment. Lowercase.

requestLost.description: Marks a cookie, or a request on the Requests tab, known only from its response: the request went out before the extension's background process restarted, so whether it carried the GPC signal was not observed. Such a cookie is listed and not counted. Shown last on a cookie's line in a panel, in parentheses in the First party lists, in place of the signal mark on a Requests row, and as the Sec-GPC value in a request's detail. Lowercase. A limit of the capture, not a fact about the site.

vdetailCookiesCapped.message: More cookies were set than the extension can list. This list is incomplete.
vdetailCookiesCapped.description: Note at the end of a vendor panel's cookie list, or after either First party list, when the list is full and the rest were left out. A limit of the extension, not an absence on the page and not a finding.

vdetailConsentCalls.description: Label in the expanded vendor panel for consent API calls made by this vendor's own script, with a count per API. Always shown, even with none, because this row is the evidence behind the vendor's GPC state.

vdetailLoadedBy.description: Section heading in the expanded vendor panel, above one line per loader the insertion records resolved for this vendor. Sibling of 'Hostnames' and 'Consent API calls'.

vdetailDomains.description: Label in the expanded vendor panel for the hostnames this vendor was contacted on.

vdetailPartitioned.description: Cookie attribute (CHIPS). A partitioned cookie is keyed to the top-level site and cannot build a cross-site profile. Reported as a plain attribute, not as an exemption: whether that difference makes a disclosure lawful is a legal conclusion this extension does not draw. Keep the technical term.

vdetailSameSite.description: Attribute name shown before a cookie's SameSite value, as 'SameSite=None'. 'SameSite' is the HTTP attribute's name: never translate it or its values (None, Lax, Strict).

reqFilterAdvertising.description: Requests filter: third-party requests to domains Disconnect's list files under Advertising. One half of the rule the cookie count uses, so the tab and the Overview agree on what is counted. Lowercase, like the other filters.

reqFilterAnalytics.description: Requests filter: third-party requests to domains Disconnect's list files under Analytics. The other half of the rule the cookie count uses. Lowercase, like the other filters.

detailRequest.description: Label in the expanded request detail, over the method and resource type.

detailSetCookie.description: Label over the cookie names this response set. Keep the HTTP header name as-is.

cookieCountedUnder.description: After a counted cookie name in a request's detail on the Requests tab, and in a tag container's panel: the company and category the count charges the cookie to. Shown where the row does not already say it, such as a cookie written by code inside the container of the company that uses that name. $COMPANY$ is the company name from the classification list and $CATEGORY$ its category label, already translated. Not a claim about who wrote the code.

detailNotStored.description: Label on a request's detail, over the names of cookies this response set that the browser's cookie jar did not hold when the extension checked, a moment after: the browser did not store them (their SameSite, Secure or Domain attributes, or a request sent without cookies) or they were removed before the check. They count nowhere. Keep it short: the value beside it is the cookie names.

detailRedirect.description: Label shown only for redirect responses.

detailRedirectValue.description: Value beside the Redirect label, on a redirect that set at least one cookie the browser kept. Explains why a redirect is listed as a request of its own. A redirect that set none reads detailRedirectNoCookies.

detailRedirectNoCookies.description: Value beside the Redirect label, on a redirect that set no cookie the browser kept: none at all, or only deletions or writes the browser's cookie jar did not hold. detailRedirectValue is the one for a redirect that set cookies.

detailNoResponse.description: Status value when a request was seen but no response was captured.

detailKeptAddress.message: Only this part of the address was kept while the extension was idle. Its query and headers were not kept.
detailKeptAddress.description: Requests tab, in a request's expanded detail, under its address, for a request kept after the browser stopped the extension's idle background process. The extension keeps such a request without its query string (the part after '?', which carries identifiers) and without its headers, so the address is shorter than the one requested. Says what the extension kept, nothing about the site.

detailSignalAbsent.description: Signal value when Sec-GPC was absent. The exception worth noticing.

detailFirstParty.description: Party value: the site the user is visiting.

groupFirstParty.description: On a domain's row in the Requests tab, where a third-party domain shows its category: marks the site's own domain. Follows the company's name where the classification list names an owner for the site. Capitalized like the category names around it; detailFirstParty is the same fact as a value in a request's detail.

detailThirdParty.description: Party value: a domain other than the site being visited.

detailResponse.description: Label over the HTTP status code in the expanded request detail. Means the server's answer, not the request's state.

detailWrittenBy.description: Label in the expanded detail of a cookie a page script wrote, over the URL of the script that wrote it. Replaces the Request, Sec-GPC and Response lines, which a script write does not have. Where no script could be identified, the URL is the page's or the frame's.

detailGpcProperty.description: Label in the expanded detail of a cookie a page script wrote, over whether navigator.globalPrivacyControl was true when it was written. A script write sends no Sec-GPC header; the property is the signal the script could have read.

detailGpcPropertySet.description: Value beside the 'GPC property' label: navigator.globalPrivacyControl was true when the script wrote the cookie. Lowercase, like the detail's other values.

detailGpcPropertyNotSet.description: Value beside the 'GPC property' label: navigator.globalPrivacyControl was not true (false, or absent) when the script wrote the cookie. Lowercase, like the detail's other values.

detailSecGpc.description: Label over the signal's value. The HTTP header name, used as the label so the value beside it is just the value.

detailVendor.description: Label over the company the classification list says owns this domain.

detailCategory.description: Label over the category Disconnect's list gives this domain, under Disconnect's own name for it (Advertising, Content, Consent Managers, and so on). Absent when Disconnect gives the domain no category.

category_advertising.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Advertising category: domains that display or enable ads or marketing offers. One of the two categories the cookie count includes.

category_analytics.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Analytics category: domains that collect information and may build a profile of activity. One of the two categories the cookie count includes.

category_social.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Social category: a social network's domains used on other sites. Not in the cookie count.

category_content.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Content category: domains Disconnect lists but does not block by default, for compatibility or because the company made a public commitment about its data use. It says nothing about serving files. Not in the cookie count.

category_email.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Email category: domains that commonly appear in email, such as the host of an open pixel. Not in the cookie count.

category_emailaggressive.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's sub-category of Email for domains whose blocking can change how an email or a link works. 'Aggressive' describes blocking them, not the domain. Not in the cookie count.

category_consentmanagers.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Consent Managers category: services whose main purpose is managing consent preferences. Not in the cookie count.

category_antifraud.description: Category name from Disconnect's classification list, shown as Disconnect writes it: the list's determination, not this extension's. Translate it as the name of that category. Disconnect's Anti-fraud category: services whose stated purpose is detecting or preventing fraud. Not in the cookie count.

categoryUncategorized.description: Category label for a company Disconnect's list names as a domain's owner without giving a category, or lists only under a technique category the extension does not show (fingerprinting, cryptomining). Shown as a group heading in the vendor list and after the company's name in the GPC read rows. Not one of Disconnect's categories: it says the list gives none. Same word as the Requests filter (reqFilterUncategorized). Never in the cookie count.

vendorsGroupUnlisted.message: No company found for this domain
vendorsGroupUnlisted.description: Heading over the vendor list's last group, after Uncategorized: one row per third-party domain the classification list names no company for. It may be the site's own content domain under another name, or a company the list does not carry; the heading claims neither. Nothing in the group is counted. Keep it short: it must fit one line at 320 pixels wide, in capitals.

markSetOneCookie.description: Marker on a collapsed request row, singular. Counts cookies the response set and the browser kept: a deletion, or a write the browser's cookie jar did not hold, is not counted here, though the detail still names it.

markSetCookies.description: Marker on a collapsed request row, plural. Counts cookies the response set and the browser kept: a deletion, or a write the browser did not store, is not counted here, though the detail still names it. $COUNT$ is the number. Singular: markSetOneCookie.

aboutVersion.description: Version line in Settings, About. $VERSION$ is the version number, never translated.

aboutLimitations.description: Settings, About group: label of the row that links to the Known limitations document.

aboutLimitationsDesc.message: What the capture cannot see, and when a number can look wrong without anything being broken.
aboutLimitationsDesc.description: Settings, About group: the line under 'Known limitations'. Says why a reader would open it.

linkLimitations.description: Settings, About group: link to the Known limitations document on GitHub. Names the destination, as linkRepo does; keep it distinct from the row label. Keep the arrow.

aboutList.description: Settings, Credits group (the last on the screen): label of the row that credits the classification list. The line under it is aboutListDesc; the links beside it are linkList and linkListLicense.

aboutListDesc.message: Disconnect's public list, version $VERSION$. Copyright Disconnect, Inc., licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. This extension compiles the list into its own index and keeps Disconnect's category names. Where several of Disconnect's categories apply to a domain, including its parent domain's, the index keeps one, and it leaves out the fingerprinting and cryptomining categories. The categories are Disconnect's. The index, and any corrections to it, are this project's. Fingerprint $HASH$.
aboutListDesc.description: Settings, Credits group: the line under 'Vendor categories'. The one place that carries the full credit the list's license requires: the creator, the copyright holder, the license, and that the data was changed. $VERSION$ is the list's date; $HASH$ is the first twelve characters of a SHA-256 fingerprint of Disconnect's file, so a disputed category can be checked against the exact file. Neither is translated. 'Disconnect, Inc.' and 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0' stay as written.

linkList.description: Settings, Credits group: link to the list's repository, beside 'Vendor categories'. Names the destination, as linkRepo does. Keep the arrow.

linkListLicense.description: Settings, Credits group: link to the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license at creativecommons.org, beside 'Vendor categories'. Keep the arrow.

aboutFunctionalList.description: Settings, Credits group: label of the row that credits the list behind the 'listed as functional' label, under the row for the classification list (aboutList). Pairs with aboutFunctionalListDesc; the links beside it reuse linkList and linkListLicense.

aboutFunctionalListDesc.message: The Open Cookie Database at commit $COMMIT$, licensed under Apache-2.0. This extension compiles it into its own list, last changed $VERSION$: it keeps the entries of load balancing and bot protection providers, drops some, and adds names from the providers' own pages. A cookie with a listed name is still counted. A second list compiled from it names the cookies each tag container's owner sets: a cookie set inside a container is counted only when its name is on it.
aboutFunctionalListDesc.description: Settings, Credits group: the line under 'Functional cookie names'. Names the source, the commit compiled, the license, and that the data was changed, as the Apache-2.0 license requires. $COMMIT$ is a short commit id and $VERSION$ a date; neither is translated. The third sentence is the rule the label rests on: a listed name never removes a cookie from the count. The last sentence credits a second list built from the same database: the cookie names each tag container's company sets.

groupCredits.description: Settings group heading, the last on the screen, over the credits for the data the extension uses (aboutList, aboutFunctionalList).

countFirstPartyVendorOne.message: Also 1 first-party cookie written by an advertising or analytics script
countFirstPartyVendorOne.description: Singular of countFirstPartyVendor: exactly one cookie.

vdetailProbeCookies.description: Vendor panel section: cookies this vendor wrote and deleted within five seconds, the way a script tests whether it can write cookies. Not counted. The values are cookie names.

hintProbeCookies.message: Written and removed within five seconds, the way a script tests whether it can write cookies. The browser kept nothing, so these are not counted.
hintProbeCookies.description: Hover text on the vdetailProbeCookies section heading.

vdetailRefusedWrites.message: Not in the browser's cookie jar (not counted)
vdetailRefusedWrites.description: Vendor panel section: cookie writes by this vendor's script that the browser's cookie jar did not hold, shown as 'name (domain)'. The browser did not accept them, or they were gone when the extension checked; for example, a script testing the widest domain it may use tries '.com' first, which the browser never keeps. Not counted.

hintRefusedWrites.message: The browser did not set these cookies or they were removed when the extension checked cookie storage a second later. They were not counted.
hintRefusedWrites.description: Hover text on the vdetailRefusedWrites section heading.

aboutLinks.description: Label of the source code row in Settings, About, beside the repository link (linkRepo). The label names the subject and the link names the destination; keep them different.

vendorsColumnCheck.description: Heading over the vendor list's GPC column, reused over the Tag containers section's. A label, not a question: the values below are the answers. 'Read' covers a call to the GPP consent API and a read of the GPC property; use the same verb as the 'Read GPC from the page' group. Its hover text is vendorsColumnCheckTitle.

vendorsColumnCheckTitle.message: Whether this vendor's own script read GPC on the page. While your GPC signal is on, the Sec-GPC header also goes out on requests to every vendor, so a vendor can receive your GPC signal without reading it from the page.
vendorsColumnCheckTitle.description: Hover text on the 'Read GPC' column heading of the vendor list. The one place that says the Sec-GPC header goes to every vendor's servers, which can act on it without any read on the page. 'Sec-GPC' is a header name: never translate it.

labelWellKnown.description: Row label in 'What this site did' for the site's /.well-known/gpc.json file, the GPC specification's optional public statement of support. The label carries the claim and the value is the site's own answer, so the site stays the speaker. Values: yes, no, not found, could not be checked, checking, check disabled. The hint under the value is the address that was checked.

valueWellKnownDisabled.description: Row value under 'Declares GPC support' when the 'Check each site's published GPC file' setting is off. Not the same as 'not found': here the extension did not look. May wrap to two lines; it names where to turn the check on.

valueWellKnownNotPresent.description: Row value under 'Declares GPC support' when the check ran and the server answered without the file, an error status included. Most sites publish no file, so this is the common case, not an error. While the check is running the row says 'checking'.

valueWellKnownUnchecked.description: Row value under 'Declares GPC support' when the request for /.well-known/gpc.json got no answer at all (a timeout, a failed connection, or a redirect whose target was never reported). Not the same as 'not found': nothing is known about the file. The hint under it is the checked address followed by hintWellKnownNoResponse.

settingWellKnown.message: Check each site's published GPC file
settingWellKnown.description: Settings switch label: whether the extension requests each site's /.well-known/gpc.json file.

settingWellKnownDesc.message: Requests /.well-known/gpc.json from each site periodically, rather than on every page. This is the only network request the extension makes, and it goes to the site you are already visiting.
settingWellKnownDesc.description: Line under the published GPC file switch. Discloses the extension's only network request, which the welcome screen also states. Gives no interval on purpose: 'rather than on every page' is the part of the promise that matters, since a request on every page would let a site recognize the extension. '/.well-known/gpc.json' is a fixed path: never translate it.

settingScriptLoading.description: Settings switch label, under Observation, on by default: record which script inserted each script on the page, so the popup can say which tag container or vendor loaded a vendor's script. Off stops only this record; the extension's other observation of the page continues.

settingScriptLoadingDesc.message: Records how scripts were added to the page, so a vendor can be traced to the tag container or script that loaded it. Stays on your device.
settingScriptLoadingDesc.description: Line under settingScriptLoading. Says what is recorded and that nothing leaves the device.

settingReadTraceCap.description: Settings switch label, on by default: limit how many GPC reads on a page are traced to the script that made them. The label names the limit, so the default reads as a limit.

settingReadTraceCapDesc.message: Limits tracing of GPC reads to a script on pages with very high read volume, to reduce the impact on page performance. When on, the first 5,000 reads are traced, then a sample up to a hard cap of 7,000. When off, every GPC read on the page is traced.
settingReadTraceCapDesc.description: Line under the 'Limit GPC read tracing' switch. The numbers are the extension's defaults; write them in your language's number format.

vendorNoCookies.description: Shown in place of cookie names for a vendor that was contacted and set no cookie. An observation, not missing data. Also on a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group whose only record is a cookie write the browser did not store; the panel shows the attempt. Lowercase.

vendorCookiesSetAndRemoved.description: Shown in place of cookie names on a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group whose only cookies were written and removed within moments, the way a script tests whether it can write cookies. The browser kept none. Plural whatever the number, as 'no cookies set' is. The panel names them under 'Written and removed (not counted)'.

vendorCookiesWithoutGpc.description: Shown in place of cookie names on a vendor row, or a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group, whose only cookies were set on requests that did not carry the GPC signal while it was on, or on lost requests, in any mix. The panel lists them, each marked 'request without GPC' (vdetailCookieUnsigned) or 'request lost' (requestLost); use the same words. Plural whatever the number. If all were on lost requests, vendorCookiesRequestLost is shown instead.

vendorCookiesRequestLost.description: Shown in place of cookie names on a vendor row, or a row in the 'No company found for this domain' group, whose only cookies were set on responses whose requests were lost when the extension's background process restarted: whether those requests carried the GPC signal was not observed. The panel lists them, each marked 'request lost'.

reportTitleFinding.description: Title of the finding report screen. Same words as the button that opens it (btnLooksWrong).

reportTitleBug.description: Title of the confirmation screen for a bug report.

reportTitleFeature.description: Title of the confirmation screen for a feature request.

reportIntroFinding.message: Tell us about anything that looks wrong, even if you are not sure. Your report helps us investigate and keep what we show accurate. This opens a prefilled issue on the project's public GitHub issue tracker.
reportIntroFinding.description: Opening paragraph of the finding report screen. Asks for a report of anything that looks wrong, then says what the button does. reportStep1 follows in the same paragraph. 'Us' and 'we' are the makers of the extension.

reportIntroBug.message: Opens a prefilled issue with your extension version, browser, list versions and settings. Nothing about the pages you have visited is included.
reportIntroBug.description: Opening line of the bug report screen; the same words as settingReportBugDesc. Says what the issue carries; the second sentence states that no page data is included, which the preview list cannot show.

reportIntroFeature.message: Opens a prefilled issue with your extension version. Nothing about the pages you have visited is included.
reportIntroFeature.description: Opening line of the feature request screen, in the same form as reportIntroBug. A feature request carries the extension version only.

reportIncludes.description: Heading over the list of everything the report discloses.

btnExport.description: Button at the foot of the popup, beside btnLooksWrong. Opens the download screen, where the page's record is saved as a file. Nothing is sent anywhere.

reportTitleExport.description: Title of the download screen. Repeats the button that opened it.

reportIntroExport.message: Download a record of what this page did.
reportIntroExport.description: Opening line of the download screen. One sentence.

exportSave.description: Button on the download screen. Saves the log, without cookie values, as a JSON file. Names the content first and the format second: the files hold different things.

exportSaveHint.message: Every request, cookie names and attributes, addresses without query strings (a tag container's id is kept). No cookie values.
exportSaveHint.description: Line under the 'Save log (JSON)' button, always visible. Says what the log holds and what it leaves out. 'Addresses' are the web addresses (URLs) of requests. A tag container's id is the one part of a query string that is kept, as reportStep1 also says.

exportSaveUnmasked.description: Third button on the download screen, never the primary one. Saves the log as a JSON file with nothing masked: cookie values, Cookie and Authorization header values, and full addresses with their query parameters. 'Sensitive information' names all of them at once; the line under the button lists them. The only way any of them reaches a file.

exportSaveUnmaskedHint.message: Adds cookie values, Cookie and Authorization header values, and full addresses including query parameters. Anyone with these values can sign in as you, so keep the file private.
exportSaveUnmaskedHint.description: Line under the 'Save log with sensitive information (JSON)' button, always visible. Must name exactly what the file adds and say that the file is sensitive. 'Cookie' and 'Authorization' are the names of HTTP request headers; keep them as they are. 'Addresses' are the web addresses (URLs) of requests.

reportCancel.description: Button dismissing the report confirmation without opening anything.

reportOpen.description: Button that copies the bundle and opens the prefilled issue.

previewSite.description: Preview row label: the site the disputed finding concerns.

previewBrowser.description: Preview row label: browser and operating system.

previewList.description: Preview row label: the classification list's source and version.

previewRequests.description: Preview row label: request count and vendor count.

previewRequestsValue.description: Value beside the 'Requests observed' preview label: $COUNT$ is the number of requests and $VENDORS$ the number of vendors that received them.

previewCookies.description: Preview row label. The value states that names are included and values are not.

previewCookieNames.description: Value beside the 'Cookies' preview label: $COUNT$ is how many distinct cookie names the report or export carries. It carries no cookie values.

previewPageData.description: Preview row label on bug and feature reports. Its value, previewPageDataNone, states that no page data is included.

previewPageDataNone.description: Value beside the 'Page data' label on a bug or feature report. Stated positively rather than left to inference: that no page data travels with these two report kinds is the property a reader most needs to be sure of.

groupFeedback.description: Settings group heading over the bug and feature report rows.

settingReportBugDesc.message: Opens a prefilled issue with your extension version, browser, list versions and settings. Nothing about the pages you have visited is included.
settingReportBugDesc.description: Line under 'Report a bug' in Settings. Says exactly what a bug report carries (the extension version, the browser and operating system, the list versions and every setting) and that nothing about visited pages is included. Same words as reportIntroBug.

settingReportFeatureDesc.message: Opens a prefilled issue on the project's public issue tracker.
settingReportFeatureDesc.description: Line under 'Suggest a feature' in Settings.

settingReportOpen.description: Button on the settings feedback rows.

reportCopied.description: Replaces the copy button's label briefly after a successful copy, so the person knows the step is done.

reportStep1.message: Optionally, you can include the findings in the issue: click $LINK$ to copy them to your clipboard, then paste them at the bottom of the issue. This will share the page's address and request URLs without their query strings (a tag container's id is kept), domains, cookie names and attributes (no cookie values), the privacy strings the page set, and your browser version.
reportStep1.description: Follows reportIntroFinding in the same paragraph, above the buttons. $LINK$ is a link whose text is reportStep1Link; pressing it copies the findings. Says the findings are optional and lists what they share, which is everything the masked record keeps. A tag container's id is the one part of a query string that is shared, and must stay in the list. 'Privacy strings' names the popup section.

reportStep1Link.description: The linked word inside reportStep1. Pressing it copies the findings to the clipboard.

reportCopyFailed.message: Couldn't copy to the clipboard. Try again.
reportCopyFailed.description: Shown when the clipboard write does not succeed. A silent failure would leave the person pasting nothing into an issue that asks for a bundle.

reportDownload.description: Button that saves the complete evidence bundle as a file for attaching to the issue.

reportStep3.message: The copied findings cover $KEPT$ of $TOTAL$ requests, because GitHub limits an issue to 65,536 characters. To include all of them, save this file and drag it into the issue.
reportStep3.description: Shown on the finding report only when the copied findings had to be shortened. States the limit as GitHub's. $KEPT$ and $TOTAL$ are request counts. Write 65,536 in your language's number format.

reportStep3Details.message: The copied findings leave out the cookie details, because GitHub limits an issue to 65,536 characters. To include all of them, save this file and drag it into the issue.
reportStep3Details.description: In place of reportStep3 when every request fit and only the per-cookie details (expiry, SameSite and the rest) were left out to stay under the limit. The counts and findings are in the copied text either way.

reportStep3Both.message: The copied findings cover $KEPT$ of $TOTAL$ requests and leave out the cookie details, because GitHub limits an issue to 65,536 characters. To include all of them, save this file and drag it into the issue.
reportStep3Both.description: In place of reportStep3 when both requests and cookie details had to be cut to stay under the limit. $KEPT$ and $TOTAL$ are request counts.

reportStep3Scripts.message: The copied findings leave out part of the record of how scripts were loaded, because GitHub limits an issue to 65,536 characters. To include all of it, save this file and drag it into the issue.
reportStep3Scripts.description: Shown on the finding report when the copied findings kept every request and the cookie details, and only the record of script loading was cut to fit. States the limit as GitHub's.

sourceNeedsReload.description: Tag after the signal status line when sending is on but this page loaded before it was turned on, so the page did not get the signal. Not the same as sourceOffInSettings, which would state the opposite of the setting. Lowercase; it continues the line.

cookieSentBack.description: Cookie attribute: this cookie was observed going back to the domain that set it, on a later request. Yes or no, never a count. Lowercase.

cookieNotSentBack.description: Cookie attribute: this cookie was not observed going back during this capture. Limited to what the capture saw, like every value in the panel. Lowercase.

cookieListedFunctional.description: Label on a counted cookie whose name is on a list of functional cookie names (load balancing and bot protection). Shown after the name and a small server icon on a vendor row, and as the cookie's last attribute in its panel. 'Listed as', never 'is': the extension reads no cookie values, so the name is all it has. The cookie is still counted. Never use words like 'safe', 'necessary' or 'harmless'. The list is credited in Settings, Credits (aboutFunctionalList). Lowercase.

cookieListedFunctionalHelp.message: This cookie name matches a list of functional cookie names often used for load balancing and bot protection. It is still included in the count because how it is used cannot be determined.
cookieListedFunctionalHelp.description: Hover text and the icon's accessible name wherever 'listed as functional' appears: on the server icon after a cookie name, on a vendor row and on the Requests tab, and on the words in the row and the panel. One text everywhere. The second sentence is why the label appears only on counted cookies.

exportSaveSummary.description: Button on the download screen. Saves what the Overview shows as a Markdown file, for pasting into a ticket. Names the content first and the format second.

exportSaveSummaryHint.message: What the Overview shows. No cookie values.
exportSaveSummaryHint.description: Line under the 'Save summary (Markdown)' button, always visible. Says what the summary holds and that it has no cookie values.

summaryTitle.description: Title line of the saved summary. $SITE$ is the site's hostname.

summaryNoSite.description: Stands in for the hostname in summaryTitle when the page has none.

summaryCount.description: Heading in the saved summary over the cookie count and the vendors that set them.

summaryAbout.description: Heading of the saved summary's footer.

summaryCaptured.description: Footer row of the saved summary. The value is the capture's date and time.

summaryScanId.description: Footer row of the saved summary. The value identifies the capture, and is the same in the log.

summaryRecordHash.message: Hash of the log without cookie values
summaryRecordHash.description: Footer row of the saved summary. The value is the hash of the masked log from the same capture, so the two files can be matched; 'without cookie values' says which of the two logs it is.

summaryLimitations.description: Footer row of the saved summary. The value is a link.

summaryCookiesSentBack.message: Sent back on a later request: $NAMES$
summaryCookiesSentBack.description: Line under a vendor's cookies in the saved summary: the cookies seen going back to the domain that set them on a later request in the same capture. The same fact as the panel's 'sent' (cookieSentBack), and never a count. A cookie not named may have had no later request, so the line never says one was not sent. $NAMES$ is a comma-separated list of cookie names, shown as code, never translated.

summaryCompanyNames.message: Company names identify their owners only.
summaryCompanyNames.description: Saved summary footer, after the statement: the vendor and company names in the file name who owns a domain or a script, nothing more.
